1737	
1738	### Goal and thesis
1739	
1740	The goal changed: **maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
1741	CAD-derived meshes**, not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
1742	operationalized as two headline numbers: the stage-2 tuned-constant count
1743	(34 at plan time; \`grep -h "^const \|^pub(crate) const \|^pub(super) const "
1744	src/stage2/*.rs | wc -l\`) and the **cliff count** — the number of constants
1745	whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model (four unrelated knobs once each
1746	flipped stepped_block medium from 83 surfaces to full per-facet collapse).
1747	
1748	The measured fragility concentrates in three structural debts, and the plan
1749	retires them in dependency order:
1750	
1751	1. **Evaluation is anecdotal.** 14 hand-watched models, Onshape/Parasolid-heavy;
1752	   three NURBS models rotted silently because nothing watched them. You cannot
1753	   claim generality you cannot measure → Phase 0 builds the instrument first.
1754	2. **Two of three tolerances are guesses.** \`--surface-tolerance\` defaults to
1755	   0.4 mm against a measured true sag of ~9e-4 mm (~400× too loose), making
1756	   centroid validation nearly vacuous; \`--angular-tolerance\` is a stand-in for
1757	   a discarded exporter setting. Both are measurable from the mesh itself
1758	   → Phases 0 (diagnostics) and 3 (regime flip).
1759	3. **One component — blind-patch seeding — forces most of the guard pile.**
1760	   \`seed_patch\`/\`condition_patch\` fit an unvalidated 32-face BFS neighbourhood;
1761	   the contamination lives on in the fit parameters, producing both the 323
1762	   NO-GROWTH seeds and plausible-but-wrong fits. Roughly two-thirds of stage
1763	   2's constants exist because tangent seams are invisible to it → Phases 1–2

1765	
1766	Everything else measured principled — stage 1, sharp-edge regions, the DOF

1770	
1771	### Phase 1 design: earned patches (replaces the blind patch)
1772	
1773	Replace grab-then-repair with **grow-under-validation**: BFS from the seed,
1774	admitting a frontier face only if it validates against the current fit at
1775	vertex tolerance; when a face fails, attempt **promotion** up the ladder
1776	(plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus), refitting accepted+candidate and
1777	requiring *every already-accepted face* to still validate; if no type
1778	validates, the face is across a seam — exclude it and record it as a
1779	**frontier face** (Phase 2 consumes these). The patch can never straddle a
1780	junction by construction, which is the exact property the blind patch lacks.
1781	Commit semantics do not change: the earned (type, params, patch) goes to the
1782	unchanged \`grow_from\` flood/refit path, and every existing commit gate
1783	(\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, torus ratio, \`MIN_*_FACES\`, \`resolve_claims\`) keeps
1784	its meaning.
1785	
1786	What makes promotion workable at tiny support — where a free least-squares fit
1787	is hopeless (sagitta arithmetic: over a 7.5° arc on r = 0.5 the sag is
1788	~0.001 mm against a 2e-5 mm quantum, so a free radius is ~2% ≈ 200× vtol
1789	wrong) — is that **facet normals are exact** and give closed-form,
1790	DOF-reducing initializers:
1791	
1792	- **Cylinder — axis = n₁ × n₂.** A planar facet spanning two rulings of a
1793	  cylinder has its normal exactly perpendicular to the axis, at any coarseness,
1794	  so two facets with non-parallel normals give the axis exactly on
1795	  strip/quad-tessellated surfaces. Radius+origin then come from
1796	  \`fit_circle_for_axis\` (cylindrical.rs), measured well-conditioned on short
1797	  arcs (r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 from 65°/60°/40° arcs). **Provenance
1798	  caveat:** a general Delaunay triangle's normal is *not* exactly
1799	  perpendicular to the axis; measure axis error per provenance (Phase 0's OCCT
1800	  meshes), and degrade to the normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
1801	  where needed — still clean, still not blind.
1802	- **Sphere — concurrent normal lines.** For any planar facet inscribed in a
1803	  sphere, the line through the facet's **circumcenter** along its normal
1804	  passes exactly through the sphere centre (equidistance). Two facets → centre
1805	  at the near-intersection (common-perpendicular midpoint), radius = distance.
1806	- **Cone** — the existing normal-covariance axis (\`smallest_eigenvector_3x3\`)
1807	  over the earned patch, guarded by \`axis_normals_consistent\`, both existing.
1808	- **Torus — meridian coplanarity, the "open case" closed.** Every torus
1809	  normal line lies in the meridian plane through its point, which contains
1810	  the axis — so each facet contributes one coplanarity constraint
1811	  \`(pᵢ − a) · (nᵢ × d) = 0\` on the axis (point a, direction d; 4 DOF; the
1812	  system is bilinear — solve by alternation or pairwise elimination). Four
1813	  facets pin the axis; then (R, r) is a 2-D circle fit in (ρ, z) profile
1814	  coordinates — \`fit_circle_2d\` already exists (toroidal.rs). **Caveats:**
1815	  rank-deficient by construction on sphere data (any axis through the centre
1816	  satisfies it) and consistent-but-degenerate on cylinder data, so ladder
1817	  order and a conditioning floor must precede it; grid-aligned quads give
1818	  near-exact meridian normals, Delaunay triangles do not. **Time-boxed**: unit
1819	  test to ~1e-9 on synthetic tori before integrating; if conditioning does not
1820	  pan out, skip it — direct torus seeding stays as today and Phase 1 is not
1821	  blocked.
1822	
1823	Two behaviours need more than validation failure:
1824	
1825	- **Ambiguity → branch, don't choose.** Two same-height faces of a cylinder
1826	  validate as a sphere centred on the axis (the hole→sphere trap at patch
1827	  scale). Grow both branches; the false one should die within a face or two
1828	  (the next face at a different height is off the sphere by ≈ Δ²/2R ≫ vtol).
1829	  Instrument branch lifetime; persistent branches mean validation is less
1830	  sharp than believed — stop and ask.
1831	- **Bent tube → drift-triggered promotion.** A bend is locally a valid
1832	  cylinder (sag of the bend over a 2 mm patch at R = 14 is ~3.6e-5 mm), so
1833	  admission never fails and promotion never triggers on residual. The signal
1834	  is **systematic fit drift**: along a straight tube successive refits are
1835	  stationary; along a bend the fitted axis precesses with a consistent sign as
1836	  support accumulates. Test drift as sign-consistency of successive axis
1837	  deltas, *not* magnitude (a magnitude bar would be a new tuned constant —
1838	  stop and ask if one seems needed). Success retires \`promote_bend\` and the
1839	  \`BEND_*\` constants; failure keeps them, and that is fine.
1840	
1841	**Deleted when this lands (after ablation evidence):** \`condition_patch\`
1842	entirely, \`seed_patch\`'s jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`,
1843	\`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`, likely
1844	\`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\` (multiple flood starts exist because the fit patch was
1845	unreliable).
1846	
1847	### Reference labeling, and what it settled (Phase 1.0, 2026-07-30)
1848	
1849	\`src/reference.rs\` (\`--reference-report\`) labels every mesh face with the
1850	reference face it came from and scores the mesh against that ground truth.
1851	Step-by-step numbers are in TODO.md 1.0; what belongs here is why it exists,
1852	why it is nearly free, and the four results that change later phases.
1853	
1854	**It is a read-back, not a new computation.** Stage 1's \`--compare\` already runs
1855	\`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\` from every mesh face centroid to a compound of the
1856	reference's faces. That call already determines which reference face won and at
1857	what (u,v); \`min_distance_to_shape\` was returning only the distance and dropping
1858	both. \`SupportOnShape2\` hands the winner back, so ground-truth labeling of the
1859	entire mesh costs one accessor call per face that was already being computed.
1860	The alternative that was on the table — a standalone probe — would have cost far
1861	more than that and measured the wrong object: it reads raw STL triangles, where
1862	the pipeline's mesh has been repaired and quad-fused, which is why
1863	\`step_measure_tolerance\` needed a \`--quad\` flag bolted on. **The general lesson
1864	is that a measurement belongs where the computation already happens**, and the
1865	same investigation found the cost of ignoring it: \`step_measure_tolerance\` still
1866	measures against the reference *solid*, so it silently reports exactly 0 for any
1867	deviation over OCCT's hard-coded 1 µm classifier tolerance (\`aTolerance = 0.001\`
1868	in \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`'s \`SolidTreatment\`) and is correct below it —
1869	exact where the answer does not matter, zero where it does. That is the same
1870	"never measure a distance against a solid" defect fixed in the pipeline on
1871	2026-07-29, in the one place the fix did not reach. It also refines that entry:
1872	the old stage-1 centroid check was not vacuous on all convex geometry, only
1873	above 1 µm, which is exactly why correct models looked right and nobody noticed.
1874	
1875	**1. The closed-form axis error is \`perpendicularity error / |n₁ × n₂|\`.**
1876	Verified to 0.1% on \`pipe_elbow_10\` Parasolid medium: a perpendicularity max of
1877	0.0280° over a conditioning p50 of 0.0271 predicts 1.033°, and the measured
1878	error is 1.0342°, identical across all 348 pairs. One relation explains every
1879	cylinder outlier in the sweep, and it separates two causes that a raw error
1880	number confounds — normals that are not perpendicular, and perfect normals
1881	amplified by an ill-conditioned cross product.
1882	
1883	**2. The Delaunay caveat did not reproduce, and the reason is architectural.**
1884	The Phase 1 design warned that "a general Delaunay triangle's normal is not
1885	exactly perpendicular to the axis" and told 1.4 to degrade that provenance to a
1886	covariance axis. Measured, OCCT's re-meshes read perpendicularity p50 = p95 =
1887	**0.0000°** and axis error **0.0000°** at every density on five of six models.
1888	The reason is already recorded under "Mesh provenance and the seam assumption":
1889	OCCT's Delaunay is *constrained* by the pre-discretized face boundaries, so a
1890	cylinder's triangles still span two rulings and their normals are still exactly
1891	perpendicular. The provenance fallback is not needed. The single genuine
1892	non-perpendicular case corpus-wide is \`l_bracket_simple\` Fusion medium
1893	(perpendicularity p50 0.2740°), a small hole carrying 96 facets over 75 mm².
1894	
1895	**3. Adjacent facets are the worst possible pairing, and finer meshes are
1896	worse.** \`|n₁ × n₂|\` for an adjacent pair is \`sin(angular step)\` — measured p50
1897	0.0432 on stepped_block fine, which is sin(2.48°) and independently recovers
1898	Onshape's 2.5° setting. So the amplification in (1) is ~23× on a fine mesh and
1899	grows as the mesh refines. This inverts the natural assumption that a denser
1900	mesh gives a better closed-form fit, and it is a design constraint on Phase 1.2
1901	rather than a property of any exporter: **pair the seed with the angularly most
1902	distant admitted facet**, where the factor is 1 and the axis error falls to the
1903	perpendicularity error itself (under 0.032° everywhere in the corpus). A 90°
1904	reading, which is the max on three rows, is the fully degenerate pair of two
1905	facets on one ruling strip — no information rather than a wrong answer.
1906	
1907	**4. The torus initializer should not be skipped.** Phase 1.1 time-boxes it on
1908	the suspicion that the meridian-coplanarity system is too ill-conditioned to
1909	solve. Its residual — the quantity the solve drives to zero — measures p50
1910	**2.354e-5 mm** over 23 863 torus facets on stepped_block fine, which is the
1911	mesh's own float32 quantum. The constraint is satisfied to the limit of what the
1912	mesh can express.
1913	
1914	**The seam assumption now has a direct measurement, and it holds.** Phase 0.5b
1915	measured only half of Design Principle #2 — that mesh *vertices* lie on the
1916	reference surfaces. The other half, that a *facet* never straddles a face
1917	boundary, is what the earned patch depends on and had never been measured.
1918	Labeling gives it for free: 51 of 157 483 facets across 79 meshes disagree about
1919	their own label across their own interior, **0.032%**. The number is an estimate
1920	rather than a bound in either direction — it over-reports where a neighbouring
1921	face curves back within reach of a sample point, and under-reports a straddle
1922	confined to a facet's rim, since the samples cover the middle of a facet — but
1923	both error terms are bounded by something this small, so the conclusion survives
1924	the imprecision even though the count does not. The only recurring cluster is
1925	exactly 12 facets on \`stepped_block_toroidal\` under OCCT coarse/medium and
1926	Fusion medium/fine, absent under Parasolid and under OCCT fine; consistent with
1927	coarse facets spanning that model's known narrow flat regions, and not chased.
1928	
1929	**Segmentation scoring closes the over-segmentation hole**, which this document
1930	recorded as needing its own step. Two area-weighted, threshold-free numbers from
1931	the same labels: \`ref coverage\` = \`Σ_R max_S area(R,S) / Σ area\` is 1.0 when no
1932	reference face was split across several of our surfaces, and \`surf purity\` =
1933	\`Σ_S max_R area(S,R) / Σ area\` is 1.0 when none of our surfaces spans several
1934	reference faces. They separate the two failure directions that "over-segmented"
1935	was being used for loosely. On the case that motivated it — \`rand_filleted_box_0\`,
1936	9 surfaces against a reference 26, passing every existing gate at 6.7e-3
1937	relative volume — they read **1.0000 and 0.2201**, correctly diagnosing merging
1938	rather than splitting, where a correct model reads 1.0000/1.0000. This satisfies
1939	the standing rule about metrics: asked what it returns for a grossly wrong
1940	input, it returns something unmistakably different from a right one.
1941	
1942	**Freeform reference faces, and the property that actually governs facet-normal
1943	exactness.** The normal report initially covered only analytic reference faces,
1944	which is 32–66% of a NURBS model's area — the rest was announced as unmeasured
1945	by the \`analytic area\` figure but not scored. Extending it needed only the
1946	footpoint (u,v) that \`ParOnFaceS2\` already reports from the same distance query,
1947	plus \`GeomLProp_SLProps\` (which arrived in the bindings on 2026-07-30).
1948	\`SLProps\` is used rather than a raw \`D1U × D1V\` because it answers
1949	\`IsNormalDefined\`, and a B-spline face has poles and seams where the normal
1950	genuinely does not exist; those facets are excluded rather than scored as an
1951	error of some size. Over the 8-model NURBS corpus every freeform facet evaluated
1952	and none landed on a pole.
1953	
1954	The result is not the obvious one. Freeform facet normals are 2–3 orders of
1955	magnitude less exact than analytic ones — \`bspline_terrain\` p50 0.9396°,
1956	\`hill_with_hole\` 0.9014°, against 0.0000° for planes — but that comparison is
1957	confounded, because the corpus's freeform models are ~100× coarser per facet.
1958	Ruledness separates them better: **\`bspline_wave\`'s *extrusion* faces read p50
1959	0.0507° at 16.7 mm² per facet, while \`bspline_terrain\`'s B-spline faces read
1960	0.9396° at 0.53 mm² per facet — the 30× coarser surface is 19× more exact.**
1961	
1962	**But ruledness is necessary, not sufficient — the real condition is that the
1963	tessellation be ruling-ALIGNED.** (Raised by the user, then measured; an earlier
1964	version of this section claimed ruledness governs, which is wrong.) The exact
1965	statement: a facet on a cylinder has its normal perpendicular to the axis **iff
1966	two of its vertices share a ruling**. Parametrize the cylinder and project the
1967	vertices along the axis; they land on a circle, the facet's plane is parallel to
1968	the axis iff those projections are collinear, and three points on a circle are
1969	collinear only when two coincide. A tessellator that lays triangles *across* the
1970	ruling family therefore produces skewed normals on a geometrically perfect
1971	cylinder.
1972	
1973	Measured over the 12 cylinder-bearing models, 12 275 cylinder facets: facets
1974	with an edge on a ruling are perpendicular to a worst case of **0.0006°**, while
1975	the **25.6%** that straddle three or more rulings reach **1.0528°**. Every
1976	non-zero perpendicularity in the corpus comes from a straddling facet, so
1977	alignment is the whole story — though straddling is necessary rather than
1978	sufficient for a *large* error, since the tilt grows with a facet's angular
1979	spread and shrinks with its axial one. That also explains the extrusion number
1980	above: 0.0507° rather than 0.0000° is itself evidence that those facets are not
1981	aligned, because alignment would force exactness.
1982	
1983	Where alignment comes from: quad fusion is a **23× discriminator but not a
1984	guarantee** — 2.7% of fused quads straddle against 62.3% of triangles (a
1985	coplanar quad on a cylinder *usually* spans two rulings, but four points on an
1986	elliptical section are coplanar too). Simple geometry gets alignment for free —
1987	a plain cylinder under OCCT is 120 quads / 0 triangles, 100% aligned, which is
1988	the real reason result (2)'s OCCT re-meshes read 0.0000°, sharper than "the
1989	rulings survive as face boundaries". Straddling concentrates where a tessellator
1990	cannot lay a clean strip: \`stepped_block_toroidal\` straddles 49–53% at every
1991	OCCT density, and its narrow flat regions between fillets are exactly its known
1992	pathology.
1993	
1994	This is *better* news for Phase 1.2 than the aggregate suggested, because the
1995	test needs no ground truth. Given a candidate axis, the minimum angular gap
1996	between a facet's vertices says whether that facet's normal can be trusted, so
1997	the earn loop can **select** the facets it initializes from rather than hoping.
1998	With the amplification law, the rule becomes: pair two **ruling-aligned** facets
1999	that are **angularly distant**. For Phase 5's freeform work the consequence is
2000	unchanged — facet normals cannot be assumed reliable on a doubly-curved patch at
2001	any density, since there are no rulings to align to.
2002	
2003	**A numerical fact worth not rediscovering.** An angle assertion near 0° cannot
2004	be tightened past about 1e-6°, because it goes through \`acos\`, which near an
2005	argument of 1 turns a 1e-16 rounding error into ~1.5e-8 rad. Assert on
2006	\`|â × b̂|\` instead, which is linear in the error and resolves to machine epsilon.
2007	Measured, not theorized: an exactly-constructed strip cylinder failed a 1e-9°
2008	perpendicularity assertion at one sample out of sixteen, and the same property
2009	passes at 1e-15 in cross-product form. The reported angles in \`reference.rs\` are
2010	printed to four decimals of a degree, far above that floor, so the report is
2011	unaffected — but do not read exactness below ~1e-6° out of a number from \`acos\`.
2012	
2013	### Phase 1.1 as built: what the closed-form initializers actually needed
2014	
2015	All four initializers are exact on synthetic data (numbers in TODO.md 1.1), but
2016	three of the four constructions the Phase 1 design named turned out to be wrong,
2017	and the reasons generalize past this step.
2018	
2019	**The bilinear system was an artefact of the coordinates.** The design records
2020	the torus axis constraint \`(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0\` as bilinear in the axis point
2021	and direction, to be solved "by alternation or pairwise elimination". Writing the
2022	axis as a *line* rather than a point-plus-direction removes the bilinearity
2023	outright: with the moment \`m = a × d\`, the constraint becomes \`qᵢ·d + nᵢ·m = 0\`
2024	where \`qᵢ = pᵢ × nᵢ\` — one linear equation per facet in six unknowns, solved as a
2025	null space with no iteration and no starting guess. The identity underneath is
2026	"every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". The one caveat is

2026	"every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". The one caveat is
2027	scaling: the \`q\` block carries length units and the \`n\` block does not, so the
2028	system must be normalized to the patch's own centroid and extent first or the
2029	null space is lost in the scale mismatch rather than in the data.
2030	
2031	**A cone is not a surface of revolution as far as this solve is concerned.** The
2032	same normal-line construction is *rank-deficient on a single ring of cone
2033	facets*, and a single ring is exactly what a real cone tessellation is: a cone is
2034	ruled, so one row of quads spans its entire height, every facet centroid sits at
2035	the same axial position, and their normal lines then all meet the axis at the
2036	same point. Any line through that point satisfies the system. On a torus the
2037	meeting point slides with the tube angle, which is why the identical solve is
2038	well posed there. The lesson is that "surface of revolution" is not the property
2039	that makes the solve work — *variation in where the normal lines cross the axis*
2040	is.
2041	
2042	**The normal-covariance cone axis has a regime the plan did not account for.**
2043	A cone's normals lie on a cone of the same half-angle about the axis, so over a
2044	full revolution the covariance has eigenvalues \`cos²α/2\` (twice) and \`sin²α\`
2045	(once), and the axis is the smallest eigenvector only while **α < 35.26°**. That
2046	is not exotic: a 90° countersink is 45°, and the corpus's own \`cone_15x20\` is
2047	36.87°. Over the partial arc an earned patch actually has, the perpendicular
2048	spread is not isotropic either and it degrades before that. What replaces it is
2049	both exact and arc-free: **every facet plane of a cone contains the apex**,
2050	because a tangent plane along a ruling contains that ruling and all rulings meet
2051	at the apex — and this holds for the chord plane of a strip quad too, since two
2052	rulings still meet there. So \`nᵢ·A = nᵢ·pᵢ\` pins the apex from three independent
2053	normals, whatever the tessellation, and direction and half-angle follow from the
2054	vertex directions about it.
2055	
2056	**Facet normals are exact for directions and biased for angles.** The
2057	perpendicularity result from Phase 1.0 says a ruling-aligned facet normal is
2058	*exactly* perpendicular to the axis. It does not say the normal equals the
2059	tangent-plane normal: a strip quad's chord plane leans off it by
2060	\`n·d = sin α·cos(Δθ/2)/√(1 − sin²α sin²(Δθ/2))\`, an \`O(Δθ²/8)\` bias. Predicted
2061	1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad, and the half-angle measured 9.985° against a
2062	true 10.000° — the same 1.5e-3. Vertices carry no such bias because they lie on
2063	the surface exactly, so wherever a quantity can be taken from vertices rather
2064	than from normals, it should be.
2065	
2066	**The conditioning floor is not a model selector, and the attempt to make it one
2067	was the familiar trap.** The meridian system is rank-deficient by construction on
2068	sphere data, so it was tempting to threshold the spectrum tightly enough to
2069	reject a sphere. Measured, the separation is not available: the degenerate sphere
2070	patch reads \`l1/l5\` = 2.06e-6 and the hardest genuine torus (R = 4, r = 3) reads
2071	9.2e-4, a factor of 450 with nothing but data-dependence between them — TODO
2072	rule 5's "detector needs just one threshold" reached from yet another direction.
2073	The floor stayed purely numerical, and *structure* does the discrimination for
2074	free: a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its fitted
2075	major radius comes out ~0 and the \`minor < major\` check rejects it outright. This
2076	is what the design meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede
2077	it" — type discrimination belongs to the ladder and to validation, never to a
2078	conditioning guard.

2080	### Phase 1.2 as attempted: why the blind patch is load-bearing
2081	
2082	Phase 1.2 was to replace \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` with a patch grown
2083	under validation. It was implemented, measured over five rounds, and **not
2084	landed** (branch \`phase-1.2-earn-loop-attempt\`). Step-by-step numbers are in
2085	TODO.md 1.2. What belongs here is the shape of the result, because it revises
2086	the phase thesis rather than merely reporting a bug.
2087	
2088	**The thesis.** "Replace grab-then-repair with grow-under-validation … The patch
2089	can never straddle a junction by construction, which is the exact property the
2090	blind patch lacks." The closed-form initializers were what made this look
2091	possible: fit exactly from a handful of facets, so validation can gate growth
2092	from the first face.
2093	
2094	**What happened.** Each round removed one piece of the blind machinery and
2095	measured the consequence; each consequence was a mechanism the previous round
2096	had not predicted.
2097	
2098	1. *Validated-only growth starves.* A cone cannot be fitted from the two facets
2099	   a validated loop has when it must first decide, so it never grows. The blind
2100	   patch was solving a real chicken-and-egg: a fit needs support, and support
2101	   needs a fit.
2102	2. *Breadth-first collection is actively wrong on a developable.* A cone's
2103	   tangent plane is **constant along a ruling**, so a plane fitted to one facet
2104	   explains its neighbours up that ruling to ~5e-7 mm — well inside \`vtol\`. BFS
2105	   therefore walks the ruling, accepting coplanar facet after coplanar facet,
2106	   and produces a flat strip whose centred normal covariance is rank 0. No
2107	   curved surface can be initialized from it, ever. The loop was systematically
2108	   collecting the faces carrying no curvature information and rejecting the ones
2109	   that carried it.
2110	3. *Spread-first collection straddles junctions.* Fixing (2) by preferring the
2111	   candidate that most increases \`|n₁ × n₂|\` inverts the failure: "most
2112	   different normal" is a fair description of *a face on the neighbouring
2113	   surface*. Measured, it split every fillet of \`rounded_cube_offset_occt_medium\`
2114	   (12 cylinders → 24) and invented two spheres on
2115	   \`cone_tangent_planes_occt_medium\`. **Two different questions had been
2116	   conflated**: which faces to *collect* wants similarity, which faces to
2117	   *initialize from* wants spread. The blind patch had the first right and the
2118	   second wrong; the earn loop had the second right and the first backwards.
2119	4. *Curvature similarity is not sufficient either.* It is the right signal —
2120	   curvature distinguishes surfaces, normal direction does not — but on a
2121	   rounded cube the fillet radius **equals** the corner-sphere radius, so it
2122	   does not separate them.
2123	5. *Validation must trim, not filter.* Clearing a patch when the seed fails its
2124	   own fit cost everything: **747 of 762** earn calls returned a bare seed.
2125	   Dropping the farthest face and refitting — \`condition_patch\`'s reasoning,
2126	   that an unfittable collection is unfittable *because* its far end is on
2127	   another surface — recovered it.
2128	
2129	**The result.** The best-performing form is: collect jet-similar, walk the DOF
2130	ladder, keep the connected component the fit explains, trimming toward the seed
2131	when the seed fails. That is \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` with a ladder
2132	choice added. **The design converged back onto what it set out to replace**, and
2133	the honest reading is that the blind patch and its conditioning are doing
2134	necessary work rather than papering over a defect.
2135	
2136	Two consequences outlive the step:
2137	
2138	- **Phase 1.5's deletion list is not supported.** \`seed_patch\`,
2139	  \`condition_patch\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\` and \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\` are
2140	  load-bearing. The four fragility cliffs among them are the price of the
2141	  fit/support chicken-and-egg, not of arbitrary tuning, and deleting them on
2142	  Phase 1's authority alone would regress the corpus.
2143	- **Closed-form initializers seed least squares; they do not replace it.** The
2144	  half-angle read from facet normals inherits the \`O(Δθ²/8)\` chord-plane bias —
2145	  0.93% at a 15.65° step, ~200× \`vtol\`. Only quantities read from *vertices*
2146	  reach the validation bar, because vertices lie on the surface exactly and
2147	  facet planes do not. The cone worked only once the closed form was used to
2148	  seed \`ConicalSurface::fit_surface\` rather than to stand in for it. This is the
2149	  same lesson as Phase 1.1's "take angles from vertices, not normals", arriving
2150	  with a price attached.
2151	
2152	**What did work**, and is worth carrying into any redesign: for plane, cylinder,
2153	sphere and torus the earned patch reproduced the existing decomposition
2154	byte-identically; and **planes must keep the blind patch outright**, because an
2155	earned plane patch is by construction "the faces that validate a plane", so a
2156	single-facet plane always succeeds, is committed, and starves the 2.3(e)
2157	B-spline fallback of the coherent leftover region it needs (the NURBS models
2158	collapsed to 94/51/83 per-facet planes with no B-spline at all).

2160	### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration
2161	
2162	The 26122-face seed sweep costs 103 s on stepped_block fine and its
2163	useful-work fraction is unknown (profile first — do not build this phase's
2164	machinery if the profile says the cost is in fits or floods rather than the
2165	sweep). The principled orderings and bounds, all derived rather than tuned:
2166	
2167	- **Distance field**: per-face geodesic distance to the region boundary
2168	  (multi-source Dijkstra over the dual graph, **centroid-gap weights in
2169	  millimetres, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded meshes, which is what
2170	  \`PATCH_RADII\` existed to patch). Seed **farthest-first** (Gonzalez maximin),
2171	  replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\` — the jet-based proxy for exactly this
2172	  quantity.
2173	- **Feedback, not detection**: tangent junctions cannot be *detected* (the
2174	  measured-dead pivot; a tangent junction is locally the *smoothest* place on
2175	  the mesh — an anti-edge), but they are *discovered exactly* by Phase 1's
2176	  excluded frontier faces. Add discovered frontiers as new distance sources
2177	  incrementally. The only trustworthy edge map is the one the fits produce.

220	/// Decompose a tangent-chain region. Returns the committed analytic
221	/// hypotheses (a strict partition after claim resolution) plus the leftover
222	/// faces no hypothesis explained.
223	pub(super) fn compete_region(
224	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
225	    region: &Region,
226	    jet: &[JetField],
227	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
228	    config: &Config,
229	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
230	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
231	    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
232	    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
233	    for &fi in &region.faces {
234	        in_region[fi] = true;
235	    }
236	
237	    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
238	    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
239	    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
240	    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };
241	
242	    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
243	    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
244	    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
245	    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
246	        .map(|fi| {
247	            if !in_region[fi] {
248	                return f64::INFINITY;
249	            }
250	            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
251	        })
252	        .collect();
253	    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
254	        score[a]
255	            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
256	            .unwrap()
257	            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
258	    });
259	
260	    // Every region face seeds exactly once — \`seeds\` is a permutation of them,
261	    // which is what terminates the loop. Committing a hypothesis does NOT
262	    // remove the faces it grew into from the seed pool.
263	    //
264	    // Growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The committed
265	    // face set is always a \`flood\` output, so every member validates — but
266	    // against a fit whose parameters came from an unvalidated seed
267	    // neighbourhood, so "validated" does not mean "the right surface". Letting
268	    // those faces seed too means a wrong hypothesis can be out-competed by a
269	    // right one grown from a face it had swallowed; \`resolve_claims\` already
270	    // exists to arbitrate the multi-claims that produces.
271	    //
272	    // It also makes the long-standing claim that seed misordering "costs only
273	    // time" actually true: previously an early bad hypothesis consumed faces a
274	    // later, better seed needed.
275	    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
276	    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
277	    let mut claimed = vec![false; n];
278	
279	    for &seed in &seeds {
280	        // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
281	        // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor —
282	        // a fit grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same
283	        // surface — so it is pure cost. Faces at the margin still seed.
284	        if claimed[seed] && interior_of_claims(mesh, seed, &claimed) {
285	            continue;
286	        }
287	        let jf = jet[seed];
288	        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
289	        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
290	        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
291	        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
292	        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
293	        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
294	        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());
295	
296	        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
297	        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
298	        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
299	        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
300	            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
301	                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
302	                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
303	                    if debug {
304	                        eprintln!(
305	                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
306	                            h.kind_name(),
307	                            sweep.to_degrees(),
308	                            h.faces().len(),
309	                        );
310	                    }
311	                    return;
312	                }
313	                let better = match best {
314	                    None => true,
315	                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
316	                };
317	                if better {
318	                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
319	                }
320	            }
321	        };
322	
323	        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
324	        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
325	        let mut cone_area = None;
326	        let mut sphere_area = None;
327	        let mut torus_area = None;
328	        if a1 >= flat_eps {
329	            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
330	            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);

332	
333	            // Toroidal candidate: a direct grow from this seed (fillet tori,
334	            // bend tubes), skipped when the seed reads sphere-like — every
335	            // adjacent quad-row band of a sphere lies near some torus, so a
336	            // (κ,κ) seed's torus is at best a bogus band that loses to the
337	            // sphere anyway. A torus seed reads |κ2| < |κ1| (κ2 varies
338	            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the
339	            // degenerate R≈r hole of a donut — a whole-region ladder case,
340	            // not a competition case).
341	            let mut torus = if a2 < 0.8 * a1 {
342	                let patch = seed_patch(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet);
343	                torus_candidate(mesh, &in_region, &patch, &[seed], centroids, config)
344	            } else {
345	                None
346	            };
347	            // Bent-tube promotion: a cylinder that stalled against
348	            // tube-continuation faces is the developable prefix of a bent
349	            // tube; grow a torus from the pure-bend patch past the stall.
350	            if let Some((cyl, _, cyl_faces)) = cone.as_ref() {
351	                if cyl.is_cylinder() {
352	                    let promoted =
353	                        promote_bend(mesh, &in_region, cyl, cyl_faces, jet, centroids, config);
354	                    if let Some(p) = promoted {
355	                        if torus.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, a, _)| p.1 > *a) {
356	                            torus = Some(p);
357	                        }
358	                    }
359	                }
360	            }
361	            torus_area = torus.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

363	            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
364	            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
365	            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
366	                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
367	                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
368	                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
369	            }
370	            consider(torus.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h), a)), 3, &mut best);
371	        }
372	        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
373	        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);
374	
375	        if debug && best.is_none() {
376	            eprintln!(
377	                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?} torus {torus_area:?})",
378	                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
379	            );
380	        }
381	
382	        if let Some((hyp, area, dof)) = best {
383	            if debug {
384	                eprintln!(
385	                    "    compete: seed {seed} → {} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof}, sweep {:.1}\u{00b0})",
386	                    hyp.kind_name(),
387	                    hyp.faces().len(),

389	                        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(t) => torus_sweep(mesh, t).to_degrees(),

393	                );
394	            }
395	            let idx = committed.len();
396	            for &f in hyp.faces() {

398	                claimed[f] = true;

400	            committed.push(hyp);
401	        }
402	        // A seed that grows nothing analytic costs only its own turn.
403	    }
404	
405	    resolve_claims(
406	        mesh,
407	        &region.faces,
408	        &mut committed,
409	        &claim_lists,
410	        config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
411	        config,
412	    )
413	}

415	/// Resolve multi-claimed faces to their best-fitting claimant (2× margin to
416	/// leave the larger claimant), rebuild each hypothesis's face/vertex lists,
417	/// drop hypotheses that lost all faces, and collect unclaimed leftovers.
418	/// Is every neighbour of \`fi\` claimed too? Such a face is interior to the
419	/// explained set and cannot seed anything new.
420	fn interior_of_claims(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, claimed: &[bool]) -> bool {
421	    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
422	    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
423	    face.neighbors[..vc]
424	        .iter()
425	        .all(|&ni| ni < 0 || claimed[ni as usize])
426	}
427	
428	/// Grow a cylinder whose axis DIRECTION is supplied by an already-committed
429	/// neighbour instead of being estimated from an unvalidated seed neighbourhood.
430	///
431	/// This is the point of stage 2.3(d2). A free 5-DOF cylinder fit on a leftover
432	/// arc fails on the **axis**, not the radius: measured on the three fillet
433	/// cylinders \`stepped_block_toroidal\` fine loses, fixing only the axis
434	/// direction recovers r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 against true 1.0 / 1.0 /
435	/// 0.5, with residuals five to ten times *under* vertex tolerance. With the
436	/// axis fixed the fit is a 3-DOF circle in the perpendicular plane, which is
437	/// well conditioned on a short arc — so growth can start from the seed facet
438	/// alone and there is no blind patch to straddle a junction.
439	pub(super) fn grow_with_axis(
440	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
441	    in_region: &[bool],
442	    seed: usize,
443	    axis: [f64; 3],
444	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
445	    config: &Config,
446	) -> Option<(ConicalHypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
447	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
448	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
449	    let mut accepted = vec![seed];
450	    let mut fit = None;
451	    for _ in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
452	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
453	        let (center, radius) =
454	            super::cylindrical::fit_circle_for_axis(&axis, &verts, &mesh.vertices)?;
455	        let mut f = ConeFit {
456	            apex: center,
457	            axis_direction: axis,
458	            half_angle: 0.0,
459	            radius,
460	            convex: None,
461	        };
462	        ConicalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut f);
463	        let grown = flood::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, &f, centroids, vtol, stol);
464	        if grown.is_empty() {
465	            return None; // the seed does not lie on its own constrained fit
466	        }
467	        let done = grown.len() == accepted.len();
468	        accepted = grown;
469	        fit = Some(f);
470	        if done {
471	            break;
472	        }
473	    }
474	    let fit = fit?;
475	    if accepted.len() < MIN_CYLINDER_FACES {
476	        return None;
477	    }
478	    let area: f64 = accepted
479	        .iter()
480	        .map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices))
481	        .sum();
482	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
483	    let hyp = ConicalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, accepted.clone(), verts, &fit);
484	    Some((hyp, area, accepted))
485	}
486	
487	fn resolve_claims(
488	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
489	    region_faces: &[usize],
490	    committed: &mut Vec<CompeteHyp>,
491	    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
492	    vtol: f64,
493	    config: &Config,
494	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
495	    let hyp_area: Vec<f64> = committed
496	        .iter()
497	        .map(|h| h.faces().iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum())
498	        .collect();
499	
500	    let mut assigned: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); committed.len()];
501	    let mut leftovers: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
502	
503	    for &fi in region_faces {
504	        let claimants = &claim_lists[fi];
505	        if claimants.is_empty() {
506	            leftovers.push(fi);
507	            continue;
508	        }
509	        if claimants.len() == 1 {
510	            assigned[claimants[0]].push(fi);
511	            continue;
512	        }
513	        let dist = |ci: usize| max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[ci], fi);
514	        // Among claimants that ALREADY explain the face within vertex
515	        // tolerance, prefer the simplest surface (lowest DOF), then largest
516	        // area, then lowest index: a face on both a cylinder and a torus near
517	        // their tangency is the cylinder's; a face on a real fillet and a
518	        // spurious thin junction torus (both sub-micron) is the larger
519	        // fillet's. Comparing absolute best-fit here instead would let a tiny
520	        // tighter sliver steal it and fragment one surface into a chain.
521	        let within: Vec<usize> = claimants.iter().copied().filter(|&ci| dist(ci) <= vtol).collect();
522	        let winner = if !within.is_empty() {
523	            *within
524	                .iter()
525	                .min_by(|&&a, &&b| {
526	                    committed[a]
527	                        .dof_rank()
528	                        .cmp(&committed[b].dof_rank())
529	                        .then_with(|| hyp_area[b].partial_cmp(&hyp_area[a]).unwrap())
530	                        .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
531	                })
532	                .unwrap()
533	        } else {
534	            // No claimant fits within tolerance — best-fit, with a 2× margin
535	            // to leave the larger-area claimant (a true junction face fits
536	            // both sides equally; the margin prevents flapping).
537	            let mut order: Vec<usize> = claimants.clone();
538	            order.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
539	                hyp_area[b].partial_cmp(&hyp_area[a]).unwrap().then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
540	            });
541	            let mut winner = order[0];
542	            let mut winner_d = dist(winner);
543	            for &ci in &order[1..] {
544	                let d = dist(ci);
545	                if d * 2.0 < winner_d {
546	                    winner = ci;
547	                    winner_d = d;
548	                }
549	            }
550	            winner
551	        };
552	        assigned[winner].push(fi);
553	    }
554	
555	    let mut out = Vec::new();
556	    for (ci, mut hyp) in committed.drain(..).enumerate() {
557	        let faces = std::mem::take(&mut assigned[ci]);
558	        if faces.is_empty() {
559	            continue;
560	        }
561	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
562	        hyp.set_faces(faces, verts);
563	        // The fit was computed on the support the flood grew, which included
564	        // every face this hypothesis could reach — junction rows it has now
565	        // lost to a better claimant among them. Those rows are exactly the ones
566	        // that pull a fit off true, so a hypothesis that has just been trimmed
567	        // is carrying the error of faces it no longer owns. Refit on what it
568	        // actually kept. (Measured on rounded_cube fine, whose r = 2 edge
569	        // fillets read 1.9976–1.9984 with no vertex closer than 5e-4 mm to
570	        // their own surface, against a mesh whose vertices are 1.9e-6 mm from
571	        // the true CAD surfaces; refitting takes them to 2.0000.)
572	        refit_in_place(mesh, &mut hyp, config);
573	        out.push(hyp);
574	    }
575	    (out, leftovers)
576	}
577	
578	
579	/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing
580	/// fit if the fitter cannot produce one.
581	fn refit_in_place(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &mut CompeteHyp, config: &Config) {
582	    let faces = hyp.faces().to_vec();
583	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
584	    let v = config.verbosity;
585	    match hyp {
586	        CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
587	            if let Some(fit) = PlanarSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
588	                *h = PlanarSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
589	            }
590	        }
591	        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
592	            if let Some(mut fit) = ConicalSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
593	                ConicalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
594	                *h = ConicalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
595	            }
596	        }
597	        CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => {
598	            if let Some(mut fit) = SphericalSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
599	                SphericalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
600	                *h = SphericalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
601	            }
602	        }
603	        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => {
604	            if let Some(mut fit) = ToroidalSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
605	                ToroidalSurface::determine_convexity(mesh, &faces, &mut fit);
606	                *h = ToroidalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
607	            }
608	        }
609	    }
610	}
611	
612	/// Grow a hypothesis of type \`S\` from \`seed\`: condition an initial fit on a
613	/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
614	/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
615	/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
616	fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
617	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
618	    in_region: &[bool],
619	    seed: usize,
620	    jet: &[JetField],
621	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
622	    config: &Config,
623	    min_faces: usize,
624	) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
625	    let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
626	    grow_from::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, patch, centroids, config, min_faces)
627	}
628	
629	/// The grow loop proper, from an explicit initial fit patch and flood start:
630	/// fit the patch, flood-accept every region face the fit validates, refit on
631	/// the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the hypothesis, its validated
632	/// area, and its face list.
633	fn grow_from<S: SurfaceType>(
634	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
635	    in_region: &[bool],
636	    start: usize,
637	    initial: Vec<usize>,
638	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
639	    config: &Config,
640	    min_faces: usize,
641	) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
642	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
643	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
644	    let mut accepted =
645	        condition_patch::<S>(mesh, start, initial, centroids, config, vtol, stol, min_faces);
646	    let mut prev = 0usize;
647	    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
648	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
649	        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
650	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
651	        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
652	        if comp.is_empty() {
653	            return None; // the start face does not lie on its own fit — reject
654	        }
655	        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
656	            accepted = comp;
657	            break;
658	        }
659	        if comp.len() == prev {
660	            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
661	            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
662	                accepted = comp;
663	            }
664	            break;
665	        }
666	        prev = accepted.len();
667	        accepted = comp;
668	    }
669	
670	    // Final fit + validated flood.
671	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
672	    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
673	    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
674	    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
675	    if faces.len() < min_faces {
676	        return None;
677	    }
678	    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
679	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
680	    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
681	    Some((hyp, area, faces))
682	}
683	
684	
685	/// A committed torus's minor radius may not exceed this fraction of its major
686	/// radius. Real fillets and bend tubes are slim (r/R ≤ 0.5 across the corpus:
687	/// full donut 0.3, pipe-elbow 0.5, fillets 0.15–0.2); an r ≈ R "fat" torus is
688	/// a bogus fit a flat cap or wall band accepts loosely and then wins on area
689	/// (filleted_pipe: an r/R = 0.82 torus ate an annular end cap).
690	const MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO: f64 = 0.7;
691	
692	/// How far a support sweeps around an axis, in radians: the angular extent of
693	/// \`verts\` about the line through \`origin\` along \`axis\`, taken as 2π minus the
694	/// largest angular gap between consecutive vertices, so a patch straddling the
695	/// angle origin measures correctly.
696	///
697	/// This is the observable that says whether a rotational parameter is
698	/// determined by the data at all. A surface of revolution fitted to a patch
699	/// that never goes around its axis has its radius free, and a free parameter is
700	/// worse than useless in competition: the fit becomes a super-model of the
701	/// simpler surface it should have lost to — covering everything that surface
702	/// covers, then flooding a little further on the slack — so it takes the
703	/// largest-validated-area contest every time. See \`MIN_TORUS_SWEEP_DEG\` and
704	/// \`MIN_CYLINDER_SWEEP_DEG\`.
705	fn axial_sweep(
706	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
707	    verts: &[usize],
708	    origin: &[f64; 3],
709	    axis: &[f64; 3],
710	) -> f64 {
711	    let (u, w) = super::perpendicular_basis(axis);
712	    let mut angles: Vec<f64> = verts
713	        .iter()
714	        .filter_map(|&vi| {
715	            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
716	            let d = [v.x - origin[0], v.y - origin[1], v.z - origin[2]];
717	            let (x, y) = (
718	                d[0] * u[0] + d[1] * u[1] + d[2] * u[2],
719	                d[0] * w[0] + d[1] * w[1] + d[2] * w[2],
720	            );
721	            // A vertex on the axis has no meaningful angle.
722	            (x.hypot(y) > 1e-12).then(|| y.atan2(x))
723	        })
724	        .collect();
725	    if angles.len() < 2 {
726	        return 0.0;
727	    }
728	    angles.sort_by(|p, q| p.partial_cmp(q).unwrap());
729	    let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
730	    for pair in angles.windows(2) {
731	        gap = gap.max(pair[1] - pair[0]);
732	    }
733	    (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0)
734	}
735	
736	/// Sweep of a candidate's support about the axis whose radius it determines.
737	/// Planes and spheres have no axis — a sphere's radius is pinned by any patch —
738	/// so they report a full turn and are never rejected on this ground.
739	fn candidate_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp) -> f64 {
740	    match hyp {
741	        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => torus_sweep(mesh, h),
742	        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => conical_sweep(mesh, h),
743	        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) | CompeteHyp::Spherical(_) => std::f64::consts::TAU,
744	    }
745	}
746	
747	/// Sweep of a toroidal hypothesis's support about its own axis.
748	fn torus_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ToroidalHypothesis) -> f64 {
749	    axial_sweep(mesh, &hyp.vertices, &hyp.center, &hyp.axis_direction)
750	}
751	
752	/// Sweep of a cylinder's support about its own axis. Meaningless for a true
753	/// cone, whose apex pins the axis regardless of sweep, so cones report a full
754	/// turn.
755	fn conical_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ConicalHypothesis) -> f64 {
756	    if !hyp.is_cylinder() {
757	        return std::f64::consts::TAU;
758	    }
759	    axial_sweep(mesh, &hyp.vertices, &hyp.apex, &hyp.axis_direction)
760	}
761	
762	/// Grow a toroidal candidate from an initial fit patch, trying flood starts
763	/// in order until one grows. Rejects degenerate giant-major-radius fits: a
764	/// short segment of straight cylinder fits a torus with an absurdly distant
765	/// axis (observed R ≈ 1500–3600 mm on ~100 mm models under the old BFS), and
766	/// a legitimate torus's major radius cannot exceed the mesh extent — the
767	/// same guard as the ladder's acceptance test. Also rejects "fat" tori
768	/// (\`r > MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO·R\`). The sweep guard that rejects a torus too
769	/// straight to have a major radius at all is applied to every candidate type
770	/// alike, in \`compete_region\` (see \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`).
771	fn torus_candidate(
772	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
773	    in_region: &[bool],
774	    initial: &[usize],
775	    starts: &[usize],
776	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
777	    config: &Config,
778	) -> Option<(ToroidalHypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
779	    let bb_diag = bounding_box_diagonal(&mesh.vertices);
780	    for &start in starts.iter().take(MAX_TORUS_STARTS) {
781	        if let Some((hyp, area, faces)) = grow_from::<ToroidalSurface>(
782	            mesh,
783	            in_region,
784	            start,
785	            initial.to_vec(),
786	            centroids,
787	            config,
788	            MIN_TORUS_FACES,
789	        ) {
790	            // A grow that succeeded but produced an implausible torus says the
791	            // *type* is wrong here, so stop — retrying other flood starts from
792	            // the same fit patch would only rediscover it. Extra starts are
793	            // for the case where the grow itself failed.
794	            return (hyp.major_radius <= bb_diag
795	                && hyp.minor_radius <= MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO * hyp.major_radius)
796	            .then_some((hyp, area, faces));
797	        }
798	    }
799	    None
800	}
801	
802	/// Stage 2.3(c) bent-tube promotion. A cylinder flood that stalled against
803	/// region faces whose jet continues the tube — κ1 ≈ the tube's 1/r, |κ2|
804	/// well below κ1 (the same tube swinging around a bend, not a cap plane's
805	/// (0,0) or an end sphere's (κ,κ)) — is the developable prefix of a bent
806	/// tube. Fit a torus to the pure-bend patch just past the stall line
807	/// (frontier faces plus their off-cylinder tube-jet neighbours) and grow it;
808	/// the result competes on validated area like any other candidate.
809	///
810	/// The cylinder fit itself locates the tangency — frontier faces failed
811	/// cylinder validation — so unlike a jet-class seed patch (which cannot tell
812	/// bend from straight tube: both read the same κ1) this patch cannot
813	/// straddle the junction.
814	fn promote_bend(
815	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
816	    in_region: &[bool],
817	    cyl: &ConicalHypothesis,
818	    cyl_faces: &[usize],
819	    jet: &[JetField],
820	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
821	    config: &Config,
822	) -> Option<(ToroidalHypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
823	    if cyl.radius_at_apex <= 0.0 {
824	        return None;
825	    }
826	    let k_tube = 1.0 / cyl.radius_at_apex;
827	    let grow_vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
828	
829	    // Max vertex distance to the stalled cylinder — the "past the tangency"
830	    // test (frontier faces failed the flood at exactly this tolerance).
831	    let off_cyl_dist = |fi: usize| -> f64 {
832	        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
833	        let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
834	        face.vertex_indices[..vc]
835	            .iter()
836	            .map(|&vi| {
837	                super::cylindrical::vertex_to_cylinder_distance(
838	                    &mesh.vertices[vi],
839	                    &cyl.apex,
840	                    &cyl.axis_direction,
841	                    cyl.radius_at_apex,
842	                )
843	                .abs()
844	            })
845	            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
846	    };
847	    // Tube-continuation jet signature. The κ2 bound is generous: a bend's
848	    // inner (saddle) side reads |κ2| = 1/(R−r), which approaches κ1 = 1/r
849	    // only for very tight bends; junction rows have contaminated jets and
850	    // are excluded from the fit patch either way (the flood claims them).
851	    let tube_jet = |fi: usize| -> bool {
852	        let a1 = jet[fi].k1.abs();
853	        a1 >= 0.5 * k_tube && a1 <= 2.0 * k_tube && jet[fi].k2.abs() <= 0.8 * a1
854	    };
855	
856	    // Frontier: in-region neighbours of the cylinder support that are past
857	    // the tangency and continue the tube.
858	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = cyl_faces.iter().copied().collect();
859	    let mut frontier: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
860	    for &fi in cyl_faces {
861	        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
862	        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
863	            if ni < 0 {
864	                continue;
865	            }
866	            let ni = ni as usize;
867	            if !in_region[ni] || !seen.insert(ni) {
868	                continue;
869	            }
870	            if off_cyl_dist(ni) > grow_vtol && tube_jet(ni) {
871	                frontier.push(ni);
872	            }
873	        }
874	    }
875	    if frontier.is_empty() {
876	        return None; // finished a straight pipe (or stalled at a cap/sphere)
877	    }
878	    frontier.sort_unstable();
879	
880	    // Pure-bend fit patch: depth-limited multi-source BFS from the frontier
881	    // through off-cylinder tube-jet faces. (Neighbours examined and rejected
882	    // above stay excluded — junction rows with contaminated jets would only
883	    // pollute the fit.)
884	    let mut patch: Vec<usize> = frontier.clone();
885	    let mut ring = frontier.clone();
886	    for _depth in 0..BEND_PATCH_DEPTH {
887	        if patch.len() >= BEND_PATCH_CAP {
888	            break;
889	        }
890	        let mut next: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
891	        for &fi in &ring {
892	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
893	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
894	                if ni < 0 {
895	                    continue;
896	                }
897	                let ni = ni as usize;
898	                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
899	                    continue;
900	                }
901	                if off_cyl_dist(ni) <= grow_vtol || !tube_jet(ni) {
902	                    continue;
903	                }
904	                seen.insert(ni);
905	                patch.push(ni);
906	                next.push(ni);
907	                if patch.len() >= BEND_PATCH_CAP {
908	                    break;
909	                }
910	            }
911	        }
912	        if next.is_empty() {
913	            break;
914	        }
915	        ring = next;
916	    }
917	    patch.sort_unstable();
918	
919	    // Flood starts: deepest-off-cylinder first — the faces most surely
920	    // interior to the bend (frontier faces sit on the junction row and may
921	    // not validate the torus fit themselves).
922	    let mut starts = patch.clone();
923	    starts.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
924	        off_cyl_dist(b)
925	            .partial_cmp(&off_cyl_dist(a))
926	            .unwrap()
927	            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
928	    });
929	
930	    torus_candidate(mesh, in_region, &patch, &starts, centroids, config)
931	}
932	
933	/// Connected region-faces reachable from \`seed\` that all validate \`fit\`
934	/// (vertex tolerance + centroid tolerance + orientation coherence).
935	fn flood<S: SurfaceType>(
936	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
937	    in_region: &[bool],
938	    seed: usize,
939	    fit: &S::Fit,
940	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
941	    vtol: f64,
942	    stol: f64,
943	) -> Vec<usize> {
944	    if !face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
945	        return Vec::new();
946	    }
947	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
948	    seen.insert(seed);
949	    let mut out = Vec::new();

1024	/// sits on another surface, and shrinking toward the seed is the one move that
1025	/// is monotonically local.
1026	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
1027	fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
1028	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
1029	    seed: usize,
1030	    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
1031	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
1032	    config: &Config,
1033	    vtol: f64,
1034	    stol: f64,
1035	    min_faces: usize,
1036	) -> Vec<usize> {

1038	    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
1039	        if patch.len() <= floor {
1040	            break;
1041	        }
1042	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
1043	        let mut fit = match S::fit_surface(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
1044	            Some(f) => f,
1045	            None => {
1046	                // No fit to rank by — shrink toward the seed instead.
1047	                let far = patch
1048	                    .iter()
1049	                    .copied()
1050	                    .filter(|&f| f != seed)
1051	                    .max_by(|&a, &b| {
1052	                        centroid_gap(centroids, seed, a)
1053	                            .partial_cmp(&centroid_gap(centroids, seed, b))
1054	                            .unwrap()
1055	                    });
1056	                match far {
1057	                    Some(f) => {
1058	                        patch.retain(|&p| p != f);
1059	                        continue;
1060	                    }
1061	                    None => break,
1062	                }
1063	            }
1064	        };
1065	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
1066	        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
1067	            break;
1068	        }
1069	        let worst = patch
1070	            .iter()
1071	            .copied()
1072	            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
1073	            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
1074	                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
1075	                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
1076	                    .unwrap()
1077	            });
1078	        match worst {
1079	            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
1080	            None => break,
1081	        }
1082	    }
1083	    patch
1084	}

1115	/// Depth-limited BFS around \`seed\`, optionally filtered by jet similarity.
1116	fn grow_patch(
1117	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
1118	    in_region: &[bool],
1119	    seed: usize,
1120	    jet: &[JetField],
1121	    use_jet: bool,
1122	) -> Vec<usize> {
1123	    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
1124	    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());
1125	    let seed_c = super::face_centroid(&mesh.faces[seed], &mesh.vertices);
1126	    let radius_limit = if use_jet && seed_mag > 1e-9 {
1127	        PATCH_RADII / seed_mag
1128	    } else {
1129	        f64::INFINITY
1130	    };
1131	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
1132	    seen.insert(seed);
1133	    let mut out = vec![seed];
1134	    // Depth-limited BFS (frontier by ring).
1135	    let mut frontier = vec![seed];
1136	    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
1137	        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
1138	            break;
1139	        }
1140	        let mut next = Vec::new();
1141	        for &fi in &frontier {
1142	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1143	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1144	                if ni < 0 {
1145	                    continue;
1146	                }
1147	                let ni = ni as usize;
1148	                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
1149	                    continue;
1150	                }
1151	                if use_jet {
1152	                    if curvature_class(jet[ni]) != seed_class {
1153	                        continue;
1154	                    }
1155	                    let mag = jet[ni].k1.abs().max(jet[ni].k2.abs());
1156	                    if seed_mag > 1e-9 && (mag > 1.5 * seed_mag || mag < 0.667 * seed_mag) {
1157	                        continue;
1158	                    }
1159	                    let c = super::face_centroid(&mesh.faces[ni], &mesh.vertices);
1160	                    let d = ((c[0] - seed_c[0]).powi(2)
1161	                        + (c[1] - seed_c[1]).powi(2)
1162	                        + (c[2] - seed_c[2]).powi(2))
1163	                    .sqrt();
1164	                    if d > radius_limit {
1165	                        continue;
1166	                    }
1167	                }
1168	                seen.insert(ni);
1169	                out.push(ni);
1170	                next.push(ni);
1171	                if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
1172	                    break;
1173	                }
1174	            }
1175	        }
1176	        frontier = next;
1177	    }
1178	    out.sort_unstable();
1179	    out
1180	}

1183	enum CurvClass {
1184	    Flat,
1185	    Developable,
1186	    Spherelike,
1187	}

1189	fn curvature_class(jf: JetField) -> CurvClass {
1190	    // Magnitude-ordered so a concave feature (dominant curvature negative, in
1191	    // k2) is not misread — see the note in \`compete_region\`.
1192	    let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
1193	    let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());
1194	    // Absolute floor is generous; only used to cluster the seed patch.
1195	    if a1 < 1e-4 {
1196	        CurvClass::Flat
1197	    } else if a2 >= 0.4 * a1 {
1198	        CurvClass::Spherelike
1199	    } else {
1200	        CurvClass::Developable
1201	    }
1202	}

1204	/// Curvature mismatch of a face vs its region neighbors (low = interior).
1205	fn neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, jet: &[JetField], in_region: &[bool]) -> f64 {
1206	    let jf = jet[fi];
1207	    let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
1208	    let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
1209	    for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
1210	        if ni < 0 {
1211	            continue;
1212	        }
1213	        let ni = ni as usize;
1214	        if !in_region[ni] {
1215	            continue;
1216	        }
1217	        let jn = jet[ni];
1218	        let d = (jf.k1 - jn.k1).abs() + (jf.k2 - jn.k2).abs();
1219	        worst = worst.max(d);
1220	    }
1221	    worst
1222	}

1278	/// Largest bounding-box dimension of a region's vertices.
1279	fn region_extent(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, region: &Region) -> f64 {
1280	    let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
1281	    let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
1282	    for &vi in &region.vertices {
1283	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
1284	        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
1285	            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
1286	            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
1287	        }
1288	    }
1289	    (max[0] - min[0]).max(max[1] - min[1]).max(max[2] - min[2])
1290	}

fn run(config: &mut Config, viz: Option<&VizSender>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let total_start = Instant::now();

        return Ok(());

    config.vertex_tolerance_mm = stage1::effective_vertex_tolerance_mm(config, &mesh);

    // Stage 2: Surface Fitting

    if !config.quiet {

    Ok(())
}

}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Ground truth: the reference's surfaces, as plain data
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// One reference face's surface, with exact parameters read from the STEP.
///
/// Parameters are copied out as plain \`f64\` rather than held as OCCT handles so
/// the whole ground truth is \`Send + Sync\` and needs no lifetime tied to the
/// reader.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum RefSurface {
    Plane {
        point: [f64; 3],
        normal: [f64; 3],
    },
    Cylinder {
        axis_pos: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
    },
    Cone {
        apex: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        half_angle: f64,
    },
    Sphere {
        centre: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
    },
    Torus {
        centre: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        major: f64,
        minor: f64,
    },
    /// A B-spline, Bezier, revolution, extrusion or offset surface — anything
    /// with no closed-form normal. The kind is carried so the report can name
    /// it, and so coverage can be reported honestly: a corpus where half the
    /// area is freeform should not look like one where the *initializers* were
    /// measured on everything. Normals on these are evaluated through OCCT
    /// rather than in closed form — see [\`ReferenceModel::normal_at_uv\`].
    Other { kind: &'static str },
}

impl RefSurface {
    /// A short name for grouping in the report.
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            RefSurface::Plane { .. } => "plane",
            RefSurface::Cylinder { .. } => "cylinder",
            RefSurface::Cone { .. } => "cone",
            RefSurface::Sphere { .. } => "sphere",
            RefSurface::Torus { .. } => "torus",
            RefSurface::Other { kind } => kind,
        }
    }

    /// The exact unit surface normal at \`p\`, unoriented.
    ///
    /// Evaluated at \`p\` itself rather than at its footpoint, which is
    /// equivalent for every analytic type here — see the module docs.
    ///
    /// Returns \`None\` on the surface's own degeneracies (a point on a
    /// cylinder's axis, a sphere's centre, a cone's apex), where the normal is
    /// genuinely undefined, and for [\`RefSurface::Other\`], which has no closed
    /// form — use [\`ReferenceModel::normal_at_uv\`] for those.
    pub fn normal_at(&self, p: [f64; 3]) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        match *self {
            RefSurface::Plane { normal, .. } => unit(normal),
            RefSurface::Cylinder {
                axis_pos, axis_dir, ..
            } => {
                let d = unit(axis_dir)?;
                let v = sub(p, axis_pos);
                unit(sub(v, scale(d, dot(v, d))))
            }
            RefSurface::Cone {
                apex,
                axis_dir,
                half_angle,
            } => {
                let d = unit(axis_dir)?;
                let v = sub(p, apex);
                let radial = unit(sub(v, scale(d, dot(v, d))))?;
                // Outward normal of a cone opening along +d tilts back toward
                // -d by the half-angle; at half_angle = 0 this is the cylinder
                // case and reduces to the radial direction.
                unit(add(
                    scale(radial, half_angle.cos()),
                    scale(d, -half_angle.sin()),
                ))
            }
            RefSurface::Sphere { centre, .. } => unit(sub(p, centre)),
            RefSurface::Torus {
                centre,
                axis_dir,
                major,
                ..
            } => {
                let d = unit(axis_dir)?;
                let v = sub(p, centre);
                let meridian = unit(sub(v, scale(d, dot(v, d))))?;
                // The centre of the tube circle through p's meridian.
                let tube_centre = add(centre, scale(meridian, major));
                unit(sub(p, tube_centre))
            }
            RefSurface::Other { .. } => None,
        }
    }

    /// The surface's axis, for the types that have one.
    pub fn axis(&self) -> Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])> {
        match *self {
            RefSurface::Cylinder {
                axis_pos, axis_dir, ..
            } => Some((axis_pos, axis_dir)),
            RefSurface::Cone {
                apex, axis_dir, ..
            } => Some((apex, axis_dir)),
            RefSurface::Torus {
                centre, axis_dir, ..
            } => Some((centre, axis_dir)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Read one reference face's surface parameters.
fn read_surface(face: &topo_ds::Face) -> RefSurface {
    let adaptor = b_rep_adaptor::Surface::new_face(face);
    match adaptor.get_type() {
        geom_abs::SurfaceType::Plane => {
            let pln = adaptor.plane();
            let ax = pln.axis();
            let loc = ax.location();
            let dir = ax.direction();
            RefSurface::Plane {
                point: [loc.x(), loc.y(), loc.z()],
                normal: [dir.x(), dir.y(), dir.z()],
            }
        }
        geom_abs::SurfaceType::Cylinder => {
            let cyl = adaptor.cylinder();
            let ax = cyl.axis();
            let loc = ax.location();
            let dir = ax.direction();
            RefSurface::Cylinder {
                axis_pos: [loc.x(), loc.y(), loc.z()],
                axis_dir: [dir.x(), dir.y(), dir.z()],
                radius: cyl.radius(),
            }
        }
        geom_abs::SurfaceType::Cone => {
            let cone = adaptor.cone();
            let ax = cone.axis();
            let dir = ax.direction();
            let apex = cone.apex();
            RefSurface::Cone {
                apex: [apex.x(), apex.y(), apex.z()],
                axis_dir: [dir.x(), dir.y(), dir.z()],
                half_angle: cone.semi_angle(),
            }
        }
        geom_abs::SurfaceType::Sphere => {
            let sph = adaptor.sphere();
            let c = sph.location();
            RefSurface::Sphere {
                centre: [c.x(), c.y(), c.z()],
                radius: sph.radius(),
            }
        }
        geom_abs::SurfaceType::Torus => {
            let tor = adaptor.torus();
            let ax = tor.axis();
            let loc = ax.location();
            let dir = ax.direction();
            RefSurface::Torus {
                centre: [loc.x(), loc.y(), loc.z()],
                axis_dir: [dir.x(), dir.y(), dir.z()],
                major: tor.major_radius(),
                minor: tor.minor_radius(),
            }
        }
        other => RefSurface::Other {
            kind: match other {
                geom_abs::SurfaceType::Bsplinesurface => "bspline",
                geom_abs::SurfaceType::Beziersurface => "bezier",
                geom_abs::SurfaceType::Surfaceofrevolution => "revolution",
                geom_abs::SurfaceType::Surfaceofextrusion => "extrusion",
                geom_abs::SurfaceType::Offsetsurface => "offset",
                _ => "other",
            },
        },
    }
}

/// [\`RefSurface\`] per face **in compound-explorer order**.
///
/// The order matters: [\`ReferenceModel::support_index\`] recovers a face index
/// by walking the same compound with the same explorer, so the two orders are
/// the same by construction rather than by assumption.

    compound: OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound>,

    geometry: Vec<OwnedPtr<geom::Handle_Geom_Surface>>,
    pub surfaces: Vec<RefSurface>,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Labeling
