/// Where a sample point's closest approach to the reference landed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum Support {
    /// Inside a reference face: an unambiguous label.
    Face(usize),
    /// On a reference edge or vertex. The sample is at a seam, which for a
    /// facet interior point means the facet reaches past a face boundary.
    Seam,
    /// The distance query returned nothing.
    None,
}

/// One mesh face's ground truth.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FaceLabel {
    /// The reference face nearest the centroid, if the centroid landed in one.
    pub support: Support,
    /// Distance from the centroid to the reference surface, mm.
    pub distance: f64,
    /// The centroid's footpoint parameters on that reference face, when it
    /// landed in one. Needed only for freeform normals; the analytic types are
    /// evaluated from the sample point directly.
    pub uv: Option<(f64, f64)>,
    /// True when the facet's interior sample points do not all agree with the
    /// centroid's label. An estimate of straddling a seam, not a bound: it both
    /// over- and under-reports, for different reasons — see the module docs.
    pub ambiguous: bool,
}

impl FaceLabel {
    /// The reference face index, for faces that got a clean one.
    pub fn face(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        match self.support {
            Support::Face(i) if !self.ambiguous => Some(i),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// One distance query, returning the winning support as well as the distance.
///
/// This is [\`crate::stage1::min_distance_to_shape\`] with the support read back
/// instead of discarded — the whole reason this module is cheap.
fn nearest(pt: [f64; 3], model: &ReferenceModel) -> (f64, Support, Option<(f64, f64)>) {
    let p = gp::Pnt::new_real3(pt[0], pt[1], pt[2]);
    let mut vertex = b_rep_builder_api::MakeVertex::new_pnt(&p);
    let vtx_shape = vertex.vertex();
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    let dist = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
        vtx_shape.as_shape(),
        model.shape(),
        0, // F (unused/obsolete)
        extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
        &progress,
    );
    if !dist.is_done() || dist.nb_solution() < 1 {
        return (f64::MAX, Support::None, None);
    }
    let support = match dist.support_type_shape2(1) {
        b_rep_extrema::SupportType::Isinface => {
            let shape = dist.support_on_shape2(1);
            match model.support_index(&shape) {
                Some(i) => Support::Face(i),
                None => Support::None,
            }
        }
        // The closest point on the reference lies on an edge or a vertex of it,
        // so the sample is off the end of any single face's trimmed domain.
        _ => Support::Seam,
    };
    // The footpoint's parameters on the winning face, for the freeform normals
    // that cannot be evaluated from the sample point. Only meaningful when the
    // support is a face.
    let uv = match support {
        Support::Face(_) => {
            let (mut u, mut v) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
            dist.par_on_face_s2(1, &mut u, &mut v);
            Some((u, v))
        }
        _ => None,
    };
    (dist.value(), support, uv)
}

/// The interior sample points used to test a facet's label for agreement.
///
/// The centroid plus one point halfway from the centroid to each vertex. All
/// are strictly interior, so a facet that lies wholly within one reference face
/// gives the same label at every one of them; a facet reaching across a seam
/// does not. Vertices themselves are deliberately not used: a mesh vertex *on*
/// a seam is expected and says nothing.
fn sample_points(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> Vec<[f64; 3]> {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
    let mut centroid = [0.0_f64; 3];
    for k in 0..n {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        centroid[0] += v.x;
        centroid[1] += v.y;
        centroid[2] += v.z;
    }
    let inv = 1.0 / n as f64;
    let centroid = scale(centroid, inv);

    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(n + 1);
    pts.push(centroid);
    for k in 0..n {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        pts.push([
            0.5 * (centroid[0] + v.x),
            0.5 * (centroid[1] + v.y),
            0.5 * (centroid[2] + v.z),
        ]);
    }
    pts
}

/// Safety").
pub fn label_faces(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, model: &ReferenceModel) -> Vec<FaceLabel> {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let unlabeled = FaceLabel {
        support: Support::None,
        distance: f64::MAX,
        uv: None,
        ambiguous: false,

    if n == 0 || model.is_empty() {

#!/bin/bash
# The sweep harness (Phase 0.3): every corpus model through the full pipeline
# with --compare, one machine-readable row per model, with baseline save/diff.
#
# This is the instrument the Robustness Rework is measured with. It replaces
# eyeballing tools/probe.sh output on 14 hand-picked models. See TODO.md
# ("Measurement protocol") and DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md ("The Robustness Rework").
#
# Usage:
#   tools/sweep.sh [--out FILE] [--jobs N] [--filter REGEX] [--timeout SECS]
#   tools/sweep.sh --baseline [FILE]   run, then save the result as the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff [FILE]       run, then diff against the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff-only A B     diff two existing result files
#   tools/sweep.sh --list              print the model/reference pairing and exit
#
# Defaults: --out tmp/sweep.tsv, --jobs 8, --timeout 300, baseline
# tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv (tmp/ is gitignored, so baselines stay local).
#
# Output is TSV with a '#'-comment header. Columns:
#   model    path under tests/, without the .stl extension
#   status   ok | fail | timeout
#   ref      step (compared against a reference) | none (crash-test only)
#   n        total surfaces in the final selection
#   plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline    per-type breakdown
#   edge_mm  stage 3.1 max edge-boundary distance to the reference
#   vol_rel  stage 4.1 output-volume relative error
#   secs     wall time
#   note     first error line, or empty
#
# RUNTIME CAVEAT: with --jobs > 1 the secs column is inflated by contention.
# Use --jobs 1 for any runtime measurement (Phase 2). The header records the
# job count so a diff cannot silently compare the two.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Overridable so tools/fragility.sh can sweep a stashed perturbed binary.
BREPPER=${BREPPER:-./target/release/brepper}
OUT=tmp/sweep.tsv
JOBS=8
FILTER=""
# 300 s is above every corpus model's runtime (worst: bspline_hill ~285 s) and
# below 3DBenchy's, which does not finish — the one row that is meant to read
# \`timeout\` until Phase 6.2 addresses runtime on real-world meshes.
TIMEOUT=300
BASELINE=tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv
MODE=run

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model/reference pairing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Rules, in order. Anything that falls through runs without --compare and is
# reported as ref=none, which is correct for crash-test-only inputs but is
# also how a new model with a perfectly good reference could go unmeasured —
# so \`--list\` prints the pairing for review.

find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir base stripped
    dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # A sources.tsv in the STL's own directory, keyed by full stem, wins over
    # every rule below. Generated corpora write one (tests/fusion_reexport/), so
    # a re-tessellation is paired with the reference it actually came from
    # instead of a stem search, which is ambiguous — plate_with_hole_100x50.step
    # exists under two directories — and resolves in filesystem order.
    if [ -f "$dir/sources.tsv" ]; then
        local recorded
        recorded=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$base" '$1 == m { print $2; exit }' "$dir/sources.tsv")
        [ -n "$recorded" ] && { echo "$recorded"; return; }
    fi

    # reference written next to it; <model>_occt_<density> with the original
    # reference in another directory, which tests/remesh/sources.tsv records
    # (keyed by model rather than by stem, hence its own rule).
    if [[ "$base" == *_offset_occt_* ]]; then

        bspline_hypotheses: cls.bspline,
        selected_surfaces: cls.selected,
        segmentation,
    };

    // Segmentation scoring against the reference (--reference-report).
    // Diagnostics only. This is the half that needs our fits; the mesh-side half
    // runs in stage 1. It re-labels rather than carrying labels forward, because
    // \`Config\` is immutable through the pipeline — the same reason the Phase 0.6
    // quantum clamp is applied in the driver.
    if config.reference_report {
        if let Some(shape) = config.compare_shape.as_ref() {
            let model = crate::reference::ReferenceModel::load(shape);
            let labels = crate::reference::label_faces(&output.mesh, &model);
            crate::reference::score_segmentation(
                &output.mesh,
                &model,
                &labels,
                &output.selected_face_sets(),
            )
            .print();
        }
    }

    Ok(output)
}

/// Stage2Output for the current rewrite frontier: segmentation only, no
/// hypotheses or selected surfaces (stages 3/4 are unreachable until the
/// classification ladder lands).
fn segmentation_only_output(mesh: ConnectedMesh, segmentation: Segmentation) -> Stage2Output {
    Stage2Output {
        mesh,
        planar_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        conical_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        spherical_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        toroidal_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        bspline_hypotheses: Vec::new(),
        selected_surfaces: Vec::new(),
        segmentation,
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Segmentation viz (--viz-stages=2.1 / 2.2)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const SHARP_EDGE_COLOR: [f32; 4] = [0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0];

/// Boundary-edge line segments for viz, one segment per undirected sharp
/// edge, offset slightly along the adjacent faces' average normal so they
/// sit visibly on top of the rendered mesh instead of z-fighting it.
/// Returns positions as [p0, p1, p0, p1, ...] pairs.
fn boundary_line_positions(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    ec: &EdgeClassification,
) -> Vec<[f32; 3]> {
    let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
    let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
    for v in &mesh.vertices {
        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
        }
    }
    let diag = ((max[0] - min[0]).powi(2)
        + (max[1] - min[1]).powi(2)
        + (max[2] - min[2]).powi(2))
    .sqrt();
    let offset = if diag.is_finite() { diag * 5e-4 } else { 0.0 };
```

// Local vector helpers (stage 2 shares only cross3/dot3/normalize3).
fn add(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
    [a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1], a[2] + b[2]]
}

fn sub(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
    [a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]]
}

fn scale(a: [f64; 3], s: f64) -> [f64; 3] {
    [a[0] * s, a[1] * s, a[2] * s]
}

fn norm(a: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    dot3(&a, &a).sqrt()
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Conditioning floors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Below this, two unit normals are parallel to within double-precision noise
/// and their cross product carries no direction at all.
///
/// A validity floor, not a threshold: it decides whether the axis *exists*, not
/// whether it is good enough. The quality of a well-defined axis is governed by
/// the amplification law in the module docs, which is a continuous relation with
/// no cut in it.
const MIN_CROSS_NORM: f64 = 1.0e-9;

/// Below this angular gap (radians) two of a facet's vertices lie on the same
/// ruling.

/// Not a tuned threshold: measured over the corpus the two cases are separated
/// by five orders of magnitude of empty space — vertices on one ruling differ
/// only by float32 mesh noise (p50 reads 5.551e-16 rad) while distinct rulings
/// are separated by the exporter's angular step (p95 1.178e-1 rad). Any cut
/// between gives the same answer.
pub(crate) const RULING_SAME_RAD: f64 = 1.0e-6;

/// The second-smallest eigenvalue must exceed this fraction of the largest for

```
//! `--invariant-report`: measure the DEVELOPMENT_PLAN "Invariants" section
//! against ground truth. **Diagnostics only — nothing downstream reads this.**
//!
//! The proposed invariants are statements of the form "every facet of a true
//! surface satisfies X" and "the discovered surface does not depend on where
//! you started". Both are only measurable against a reference that says which
//! facets belong to which surface, which is exactly what
//! [`crate::reference::label_faces`] produces for free from the `--compare`
//! distance query. So this module is a second consumer of that ground truth,
//! run after stage 2.2 (where the jet and the smooth regions exist) and before
//! 2.3 (whose decomposition it deliberately does not use — a fragile invariant
//! must be visible on models whose decomposition fails outright).
//!
//! Five families, matching the section's five headings:
//!
//! - **F (Fitting Requirement)** — with the reference's *own exact* surface
//!   parameters, how far off it do the facets' vertices, edge midpoints, facet
//!   centroids and facet interiors actually land, and how large is the
//!   within-surface dihedral? This asks whether the requirement is satisfiable
//!   at all before asking whether any algorithm satisfies it. It also measures
//!   the two probe choices the section makes (edge centres for developables,
//!   facet centres for spheres) against the true whole-facet maximum.
//! - **A (angular separability)** — the largest dihedral *inside* a reference
//!   face against the smallest dihedral *across* its boundary. Where the first
//!   exceeds the second, no angular tolerance can separate that pair.
//! - **I (Surface Identification)** — fit all four analytic types to the true
//!   facet set of each reference face and report each one's worst vertex
//!   residual, in millimetres and in float32 quanta. This is the distribution
//!   behind the section's open question about a cone that fits a cylinder.
//! - **S (Seed Independence)** — run the production grow (`compete::grow`) from
//!   many different seeds inside one reference face and count how many distinct
//!   face sets come back, how many equal the truth, and the worst Jaccard.
//!   Also runs the full multi-type competition (`compete::compete_from_seed`)
//!   per seed, which is what the pipeline actually does.
//! - **G (Growth Independence)** — the flood re-run with the neighbour
//!   iteration reversed (a direct test of traversal-order independence), the
//!   refit fixpoint started from the whole true face set instead of the seed
//!   patch (a direct test of start independence), and how often the refit loop
//!   hits its round cap without converging.
//!
//! Output is one TSV row per reference face on **stdout** (prefix `INV`) plus a
//! per-model summary on stderr, so a shell harness can concatenate models.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::reference::{FaceLabel, RefSurface, ReferenceModel};
use crate::stage1::{float32_position_bound_mm, ConnectedMesh};

use super::compete;
use super::conical::ConicalSurface;
use super::edges::JetField;
use super::planar::PlanarSurface;
use super::spherical::SphericalSurface;
use super::surface::SurfaceType;
use super::toroidal::ToroidalSurface;
use super::{
    face_area, face_centroid, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES, MIN_SPHERE_FACES, MIN_TORUS_FACES,
};

/// How many seeds to try per reference face in the seed-independence test.
/// Seeds are taken at a fixed stride over the face's sorted facet list, so the
/// sample is deterministic and spread over the surface rather than clustered.
const MAX_SEEDS_PER_FACE: usize = 24;

/// Reference faces with fewer facets than this are reported but not
/// seed-tested: with 3 facets there is nothing for a seed to be independent of.
const MIN_FACETS_FOR_SEED_TEST: usize = 6;

/// Barycentric sampling order for the whole-facet maximum. Order n gives
/// (n-1)(n-2)/2 strictly interior points per triangle — 21 at n = 8.
const INTERIOR_ORDER: usize = 8;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Exact distances to a reference surface
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn sub(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
    [a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]]
}
fn dot(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
}
fn norm(a: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    dot(a, a).sqrt()
}
fn unit(a: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
    let n = norm(a);
    if n > 0.0 {
        [a[0] / n, a[1] / n, a[2] / n]
    } else {
        [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]
    }
}

/// Perpendicular distance from `p` to a reference surface, or `None` for the
/// freeform types (no closed form; measuring those needs OCCT and is out of
/// scope for a per-sample-point inner loop).
fn ref_distance(s: &RefSurface, p: [f64; 3]) -> Option<f64> {
    Some(match *s {
        RefSurface::Plane { point, normal } => dot(sub(p, point), unit(normal)).abs(),
        RefSurface::Cylinder {
            axis_pos,
            axis_dir,
            radius,
        } => {
            let d = unit(axis_dir);
            let v = sub(p, axis_pos);
            let h = dot(v, d);
            let rho = norm(sub(v, [d[0] * h, d[1] * h, d[2] * h]));
            (rho - radius).abs()
        }
        RefSurface::Cone {
            apex,
            axis_dir,
            half_angle,
        } => {
            // Distance to the double cone's nearer nappe, measured along the
            // surface normal: rho*cos(a) - h*sin(a) with h along the opening
            // direction. OCCT's semi-angle is signed with the axis direction.
            let d = unit(axis_dir);
            let v = sub(p, apex);
            let h = dot(v, d);
            let rho = norm(sub(v, [d[0] * h, d[1] * h, d[2] * h]));
            (rho * half_angle.cos() - h * half_angle.sin()).abs()
        }
        RefSurface::Sphere { centre, radius } => (norm(sub(p, centre)) - radius).abs(),
        RefSurface::Torus {
            centre,
            axis_dir,
            major,
            minor,
        } => {
            let d = unit(axis_dir);
            let v = sub(p, centre);
            let z = dot(v, d);
            let rho = norm(sub(v, [d[0] * z, d[1] * z, d[2] * z]));
            (((rho - major).powi(2) + z * z).sqrt() - minor).abs()
        }
        RefSurface::Other { .. } => return None,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Facet geometry helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn vertex_pos(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, vi: usize) -> [f64; 3] {
    let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
    [v.x, v.y, v.z]
}

fn facet_points(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> Vec<[f64; 3]> {
    let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
    (0..f.vertex_count as usize)
        .map(|k| vertex_pos(mesh, f.vertex_indices[k]))
        .collect()
}

/// Unit facet normal (recomputed rather than trusting a cached one).
fn facet_normal(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> [f64; 3] {
    let p = facet_points(mesh, fi);
    if p.len() < 3 {
        return [0.0, 0.0, 1.0];
    }
    let a = sub(p[1], p[0]);
    let b = sub(p[2], p[0]);
    unit([
        a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1],
        a[2] * b[0] - a[0] * b[2],
        a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0],
    ])
}

/// Dihedral angle between two adjacent facets, in degrees.
fn dihedral_deg(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, a: usize, b: usize) -> f64 {
    let (na, nb) = (facet_normal(mesh, a), facet_normal(mesh, b));
    // Angle via the cross product, which stays linear in the error near 0°
    // (see DEVELOPMENT_PLAN: acos amplifies rounding near an argument of 1).
    let c = [
        na[1] * nb[2] - na[2] * nb[1],
        na[2] * nb[0] - na[0] * nb[2],
        na[0] * nb[1] - na[1] * nb[0],
    ];
    norm(c).atan2(dot(na, nb)).to_degrees().abs()
}

/// The three probes the Invariants section names, plus the true whole-facet
/// maximum from a dense interior sample: (vertex, edge midpoint, centroid,
/// interior).
fn facet_probes(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, s: &RefSurface) -> Option<(f64, f64, f64, f64)> {
    let p = facet_points(mesh, fi);
    let n = p.len();
    if n < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut v_max = 0.0_f64;
    for &q in &p {
        v_max = v_max.max(ref_distance(s, q)?);
    }
    let mut e_max = 0.0_f64;
    for k in 0..n {
        let q = p[k];
        let r = p[(k + 1) % n];
        e_max = e_max.max(ref_distance(s, [
            0.5 * (q[0] + r[0]),
            0.5 * (q[1] + r[1]),
            0.5 * (q[2] + r[2]),
        ])?);
    }
    let c = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
    let c_max = ref_distance(s, c)?;

    // Interior: barycentric grid over the fan triangulation.
    let mut i_max = 0.0_f64;
    let tris: Vec<[usize; 3]> = (1..n - 1).map(|k| [0, k, k + 1]).collect();
    let m = INTERIOR_ORDER;
    for t in tris {
        for i in 1..m {
            for j in 1..(m - i) {
                let k = m - i - j;
                if k == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let (a, b, cc) = (i as f64 / m as f64, j as f64 / m as f64, k as f64 / m as f64);
                let q = [
                    a * p[t[0]][0] + b * p[t[1]][0] + cc * p[t[2]][0],
                    a * p[t[0]][1] + b * p[t[1]][1] + cc * p[t[2]][1],
                    a * p[t[0]][2] + b * p[t[1]][2] + cc * p[t[2]][2],
                ];
                i_max = i_max.max(ref_distance(s, q)?);
            }
        }
    }
    Some((v_max, e_max, c_max, i_max))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Per-reference-face measurement
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Which production surface type stands in for a reference type.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Kind {
    Plane,
    Cylinder,
    Cone,
    Sphere,
    Torus,
    Other,
}

fn kind_of(s: &RefSurface) -> Kind {
    match s {
        RefSurface::Plane { .. } => Kind::Plane,
        RefSurface::Cylinder { .. } => Kind::Cylinder,
        RefSurface::Cone { .. } => Kind::Cone,
        RefSurface::Sphere { .. } => Kind::Sphere,
        RefSurface::Torus { .. } => Kind::Torus,
        RefSurface::Other { .. } => Kind::Other,
    }
}

/// Worst vertex residual of a freshly fitted surface of type `S` over `faces`.
/// `None` when the fitter declines the face set.
fn fit_residual<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Option<f64> {
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, faces);
    let fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, faces, &verts, 0)?;
    let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
    for &vi in &verts {
        worst = worst.max(S::vertex_distance(&fit, &vertex_pos(mesh, vi)));
    }
    Some(worst)
}

fn vertices_of(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut v: Vec<usize> = faces
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|&fi| {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
        })
        .collect();
    v.sort_unstable();
    v.dedup();
    v
}

/// A flood identical to `compete::flood` except that the neighbour list is
/// walked in reverse. Used only to test traversal-order independence.
fn flood_reversed<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    fit: &S::Fit,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    if !compete::face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    seen.insert(seed);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut queue = std::collections::VecDeque::from([seed]);
    while let Some(fi) = queue.pop_front() {
        out.push(fi);
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc].iter().rev() {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if in_region[ni]
                && !seen.contains(&ni)
                && compete::face_validates::<S>(mesh, ni, fit, centroids, vtol, stol)
            {
                seen.insert(ni);
                queue.push_back(ni);
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort_unstable();
    out
}

/// One reference face's measurements.
struct Row {
    idx: usize,
    kind: &'static str,
    facets: usize,
    area: f64,
    // F — fitting requirement against the reference's own parameters
    v_max: f64,
    e_max: f64,
    c_max: f64,
    i_max: f64,
    // A — angular separability
    dih_in_max: f64,
    dih_out_min: f64,
    // I — identification: worst vertex residual per candidate type, mm
    res: [f64; 4], // plane, sphere, cyl/cone, torus
    // S — seed independence
    seeds: usize,
    grew: usize,
    exact: usize,
    distinct: usize,
    jacc_min: f64,
    // competition-level (all four types compete, as the pipeline does)
    c_distinct_types: usize,
    c_correct_type: usize,
    // G — growth independence
    order_diffs: usize,
    oracle_same: bool,
}

/// Jaccard index of two sorted face sets.
fn jaccard(a: &[usize], b: &HashSet<usize>) -> f64 {
    if a.is_empty() && b.is_empty() {
        return 1.0;
    }
    let inter = a.iter().filter(|f| b.contains(f)).count();
    let union = a.len() + b.len() - inter;
    if union == 0 {
        1.0
    } else {
        inter as f64 / union as f64
    }
}

/// Run the whole report. `jet`, `face_region` and `regions` come from stage 2.2.
pub fn report(
    config: &Config,
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    model: &ReferenceModel,
    labels: &[FaceLabel],
    jet: &[JetField],
    face_region: &[usize],
    regions: &[super::regions::Region],
) {
    let model_name = config
        .input_file
        .rsplit('/')
        .next()
        .unwrap_or(&config.input_file)
        .trim_end_matches(".stl")
        .to_string();
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let quantum = float32_position_bound_mm(mesh);
    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = (0..mesh.faces.len())
        .map(|fi| face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices))
        .collect();

    // Group facets by reference face.
    let mut by_ref: HashMap<usize, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut unlabeled = 0usize;
    for (fi, lab) in labels.iter().enumerate() {
        match lab.face() {
            Some(r) => by_ref.entry(r).or_default().push(fi),
            None => unlabeled += 1,
        }
    }
    for v in by_ref.values_mut() {
        v.sort_unstable();
    }

    // Reverse lookup for the across-boundary dihedral.
    let mut ref_of: Vec<Option<usize>> = vec![None; mesh.faces.len()];
    for (&r, faces) in &by_ref {
        for &fi in faces {
            ref_of[fi] = Some(r);
        }
    }

    let mut keys: Vec<usize> = by_ref.keys().copied().collect();
    keys.sort_unstable();

    println!(
        "#INV\tmodel\tref\tkind\tfacets\tarea\tvmax\temax\tcmax\timax\tdih_in\tdih_out\t\
         res_plane\tres_sphere\tres_cyl\tres_torus\tseeds\tgrew\texact\tdistinct\tjacc_min\t\
         ctypes\tccorrect\torder_diffs\toracle\tvtol\tstol\tquantum"
    );

    let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
    for &r in &keys {
        let faces = &by_ref[&r];
        let surf = &model.surfaces[r];
        let kind = kind_of(surf);
        let area: f64 = faces
            .iter()
            .map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices))
            .sum();

        // --- F: fitting requirement against ground truth -------------------
        let (mut v_max, mut e_max, mut c_max, mut i_max) = (0.0_f64, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        let mut probes_ok = true;
        for &fi in faces {
            match facet_probes(mesh, fi, surf) {
                Some((v, e, c, i)) => {
                    v_max = v_max.max(v);
                    e_max = e_max.max(e);
                    c_max = c_max.max(c);
                    i_max = i_max.max(i);
                }
                None => {
                    probes_ok = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if !probes_ok {
            v_max = f64::NAN;
            e_max = f64::NAN;
            c_max = f64::NAN;
            i_max = f64::NAN;
        }

        // --- A: angular separability ---------------------------------------
        let mut dih_in_max = 0.0_f64;
        let mut dih_out_min = f64::INFINITY;
        for &fi in faces {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                if ni < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let ni = ni as usize;
                let d = dihedral_deg(mesh, fi, ni);
                match ref_of[ni] {
                    Some(o) if o == r => dih_in_max = dih_in_max.max(d),
                    Some(_) => dih_out_min = dih_out_min.min(d),
                    None => {}
                }
            }
        }

        // --- I: all four types on the true support -------------------------
        let res = [
            fit_residual::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, faces).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            fit_residual::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, faces).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            fit_residual::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, faces).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            fit_residual::<ToroidalSurface>(mesh, faces).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
        ];

        // --- S/G: seed and growth independence -----------------------------
        let mut row = Row {
            idx: r,
            kind: surf.type_name(),
            facets: faces.len(),
            area,
            v_max,
            e_max,
            c_max,
            i_max,
            dih_in_max,
            dih_out_min,
            res,
            seeds: 0,
            grew: 0,
            exact: 0,
            distinct: 0,
            jacc_min: f64::NAN,
            c_distinct_types: 0,
            c_correct_type: 0,
            order_diffs: 0,
            oracle_same: false,
        };

        if faces.len() >= MIN_FACETS_FOR_SEED_TEST && kind != Kind::Other {
            let truth: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
            // The smooth region the face lives in — the arena competition uses.
            let reg = face_region[faces[0]];
            let mut in_region = vec![false; mesh.faces.len()];
            if reg < regions.len() {
                for &fi in &regions[reg].faces {
                    in_region[fi] = true;
                }
            }

            let stride = (faces.len() / MAX_SEEDS_PER_FACE).max(1);
            let seeds: Vec<usize> = faces.iter().copied().step_by(stride).collect();
            let seeds: Vec<usize> = seeds.into_iter().take(MAX_SEEDS_PER_FACE).collect();
            row.seeds = seeds.len();

            let mut outcomes: HashSet<Vec<usize>> = HashSet::new();
            let mut jacc_min = f64::INFINITY;
            let mut ctypes: HashSet<&'static str> = HashSet::new();
            let want_type = match kind {
                Kind::Plane => "plane",
                Kind::Cylinder => "cyl",
                Kind::Cone => "cone",
                Kind::Sphere => "sphere",
                Kind::Torus => "torus",
                Kind::Other => "",
            };
            let flat_eps = {
                // Mirror compete_region's region-scale flatness floor.
                let mut min = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
                let mut max = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
                if reg < regions.len() {
                    for &vi in &regions[reg].vertices {
                        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
                        for (k, c) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].into_iter().enumerate() {
                            min[k] = min[k].min(c);
                            max[k] = max[k].max(c);
                        }
                    }
                }
                let extent = (max[0] - min[0]).max(max[1] - min[1]).max(max[2] - min[2]);
                if extent.is_finite() && extent > 0.0 {
                    1.0 / (2.0 * extent)
                } else {
                    1e-6
                }
            };

            for &seed in &seeds {
                // Single-type grow: the invariant as the section states it.
                let grown: Option<Vec<usize>> = match kind {
                    Kind::Plane => compete::grow::<PlanarSurface>(
                        mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, &centroids, config, 1,
                    )
                    .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                    Kind::Cylinder | Kind::Cone => compete::grow::<ConicalSurface>(
                        mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, &centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES,
                    )
                    .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                    Kind::Sphere => compete::grow::<SphericalSurface>(
                        mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, &centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES,
                    )
                    .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                    Kind::Torus => compete::grow::<ToroidalSurface>(
                        mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, &centroids, config, MIN_TORUS_FACES,
                    )
                    .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                    Kind::Other => None,
                };
                if let Some(g) = grown {
                    row.grew += 1;
                    if g.len() == truth.len() && g.iter().all(|f| truth.contains(f)) {
                        row.exact += 1;
                    }
                    jacc_min = jacc_min.min(jaccard(&g, &truth));
                    outcomes.insert(g);
                }

                // Competition-level: what the pipeline would actually pick.
                if let Some((hyp, _, _)) = compete::compete_from_seed(
                    mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, &centroids, config, flat_eps, false,
                ) {
                    ctypes.insert(hyp.kind_name());
                    if hyp.kind_name() == want_type {
                        row.c_correct_type += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            row.distinct = outcomes.len();
            row.jacc_min = if jacc_min.is_finite() { jacc_min } else { f64::NAN };
            row.c_distinct_types = ctypes.len();

            // --- G: traversal-order independence of the flood ---------------
            // Fit the true support once, then flood from each seed in both
            // neighbour orders and compare the resulting sets.
            let verts = vertices_of(mesh, faces);
            macro_rules! order_test {
                ($S:ty) => {{
                    if let Some(mut fit) = <$S>::fit_surface(mesh, faces, &verts, 0) {
                        <$S>::determine_convexity(mesh, faces, &mut fit);
                        let mut diffs = 0;
                        for &seed in &seeds {
                            let a = compete::flood::<$S>(
                                mesh, &in_region, seed, &fit, &centroids, vtol, stol,
                            );
                            let b = flood_reversed::<$S>(
                                mesh, &in_region, seed, &fit, &centroids, vtol, stol,
                            );
                            if a != b {
                                diffs += 1;
                            }
                        }
                        row.order_diffs = diffs;
                    }
                }};
            }
            match kind {
                Kind::Plane => order_test!(PlanarSurface),
                Kind::Cylinder | Kind::Cone => order_test!(ConicalSurface),
                Kind::Sphere => order_test!(SphericalSurface),
                Kind::Torus => order_test!(ToroidalSurface),
                Kind::Other => {}
            }

            // --- G: start independence of the refit fixpoint ----------------
            // Feed `grow_from` the ENTIRE true face set as its initial patch —
            // the most different start possible from a 32-face seed patch — and
            // ask whether the fixpoint is the same one the seed reached.
            let seed0 = seeds[0];
            let oracle: Option<Vec<usize>> = match kind {
                Kind::Plane => compete::grow_from::<PlanarSurface>(
                    mesh, &in_region, seed0, faces.clone(), &centroids, config, 1,
                )
                .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                Kind::Cylinder | Kind::Cone => compete::grow_from::<ConicalSurface>(
                    mesh, &in_region, seed0, faces.clone(), &centroids, config,
                    MIN_CYLINDER_FACES,
                )
                .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                Kind::Sphere => compete::grow_from::<SphericalSurface>(
                    mesh, &in_region, seed0, faces.clone(), &centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES,
                )
                .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                Kind::Torus => compete::grow_from::<ToroidalSurface>(
                    mesh, &in_region, seed0, faces.clone(), &centroids, config, MIN_TORUS_FACES,
                )
                .map(|(_, _, f)| f),
                Kind::Other => None,
            };
            row.oracle_same = match oracle {
                Some(o) => o.len() == truth.len() && o.iter().all(|f| truth.contains(f)),
                None => false,
            };
        }

        println!(
            "INV\t{model}\t{idx}\t{kind}\t{facets}\t{area:.6}\t{vmax:.6e}\t{emax:.6e}\t\
             {cmax:.6e}\t{imax:.6e}\t{din:.4}\t{dout:.4}\t{r0:.6e}\t{r1:.6e}\t{r2:.6e}\t\
             {r3:.6e}\t{seeds}\t{grew}\t{exact}\t{distinct}\t{jacc:.4}\t{ct}\t{cc}\t{od}\t\
             {oracle}\t{vtol:.6e}\t{stol:.6e}\t{q:.6e}",
            model = model_name,
            idx = row.idx,
            kind = row.kind,
            facets = row.facets,
            area = row.area,
            vmax = row.v_max,
            emax = row.e_max,
            cmax = row.c_max,
            imax = row.i_max,
            din = row.dih_in_max,
            dout = if row.dih_out_min.is_finite() { row.dih_out_min } else { -1.0 },
            r0 = row.res[0],
            r1 = row.res[1],
            r2 = row.res[2],
            r3 = row.res[3],
            seeds = row.seeds,
            grew = row.grew,
            exact = row.exact,
            distinct = row.distinct,
            jacc = row.jacc_min,
            ct = row.c_distinct_types,
            cc = row.c_correct_type,
            od = row.order_diffs,
            oracle = if row.oracle_same { 1 } else { 0 },
            vtol = vtol,
            stol = stol,
            q = quantum,
        );
        rows.push(row);
    }

    summarize(&model_name, &rows, unlabeled, mesh.faces.len(), vtol, stol, quantum);
}

fn pct(a: usize, b: usize) -> f64 {
    if b == 0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        100.0 * a as f64 / b as f64
    }
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn summarize(
    model: &str,
    rows: &[Row],
    unlabeled: usize,
    total_faces: usize,
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
    quantum: f64,
) {
    let analytic: Vec<&Row> = rows.iter().filter(|r| r.v_max.is_finite()).collect();
    eprintln!("  Invariant report ({model}):");
    eprintln!(
        "    reference faces {} ({} analytic, {} freeform/unmeasurable); \
         {unlabeled} of {total_faces} facets unlabeled (seam-ambiguous)",
        rows.len(),
        analytic.len(),
        rows.len() - analytic.len(),
    );
    eprintln!(
        "    tolerances: vtol {vtol:.3e}  stol {stol:.3e}  f32 bound {quantum:.3e} mm"
    );

    if !analytic.is_empty() {
        let worst_v = analytic.iter().map(|r| r.v_max).fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let worst_e = analytic.iter().map(|r| r.e_max).fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let worst_c = analytic.iter().map(|r| r.c_max).fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let worst_i = analytic.iter().map(|r| r.i_max).fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let v_fail = analytic.iter().filter(|r| r.v_max > vtol).count();
        let e_fail = analytic.iter().filter(|r| r.e_max > stol).count();
        let c_fail = analytic.iter().filter(|r| r.c_max > stol).count();
        eprintln!(
            "    F  vertex max {worst_v:.3e} ({} q) — {v_fail} face(s) over vtol",
            (worst_v / quantum).round() as i64
        );
        eprintln!(
            "    F  edge-mid max {worst_e:.3e} ({e_fail} over stol); centroid max {worst_c:.3e} \
             ({c_fail} over stol); interior max {worst_i:.3e}"
        );
        // The 4/3 prediction: the whole-facet max lies in [edge-mid max, 4/3 × it].
        let ratios: Vec<f64> = analytic
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.e_max > 0.0)
            .map(|r| r.i_max.max(r.c_max).max(r.e_max) / r.e_max)
            .collect();
        if !ratios.is_empty() {
            let hi = ratios.iter().cloned().fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
            let over = ratios.iter().filter(|&&x| x > 4.0 / 3.0 + 1e-9).count();
            eprintln!(
                "    F  facet-max / edge-mid-max: worst {hi:.4} (predicted \u{2264} 1.3333); \
                 {over} face(s) over"
            );
        }
        let cratios: Vec<f64> = analytic
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.c_max > 0.0)
            .map(|r| r.i_max.max(r.e_max).max(r.c_max) / r.c_max)
            .collect();
        if !cratios.is_empty() {
            let hi = cratios.iter().cloned().fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
            eprintln!("    F  facet-max / centroid: worst {hi:.4} (centroid under-reads by this)");
        }
    }

    let sep: Vec<&Row> = rows
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| r.dih_out_min.is_finite() && r.dih_in_max > 0.0)
        .collect();
    let inseparable = sep.iter().filter(|r| r.dih_in_max >= r.dih_out_min).count();
    if !sep.is_empty() {
        let worst = sep
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.dih_in_max / r.dih_out_min.max(1e-12))
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        eprintln!(
            "    A  {inseparable} of {} faces have an interior dihedral \u{2265} their smallest \
             boundary dihedral (worst ratio {worst:.1}\u{00d7}) — no angular tolerance separates those",
            sep.len()
        );
    }

    // Identification: how often does a WRONG type also validate the true support?
    let names = ["plane", "sphere", "cyl/cone", "torus"];
    let want = |r: &Row| match r.kind {
        "plane" => 0usize,
        "sphere" => 1,
        "cylinder" | "cone" => 2,
        "torus" => 3,
        _ => usize::MAX,
    };
    let mut impostors = vec![0usize; 4];
    let mut own_fail = 0usize;
    let mut n_typed = 0usize;
    for r in rows {
        let w = want(r);
        if w == usize::MAX {
            continue;
        }
        n_typed += 1;
        if !(r.res[w] <= vtol) {
            own_fail += 1;
        }
        for k in 0..4 {
            if k != w && r.res[k].is_finite() && r.res[k] <= vtol {
                impostors[k] += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    if n_typed > 0 {
        eprintln!(
            "    I  {own_fail} of {n_typed} reference faces are NOT explained at vtol by a fit of \
             their OWN type"
        );
        eprintln!(
            "    I  wrong types that also validate the true support: {}",
            names
                .iter()
                .zip(&impostors)
                .filter(|(_, &c)| c > 0)
                .map(|(n, c)| format!("{n} {c}"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        );
    }

    let tested: Vec<&Row> = rows.iter().filter(|r| r.seeds > 0).collect();
    if !tested.is_empty() {
        let seeds: usize = tested.iter().map(|r| r.seeds).sum();
        let grew: usize = tested.iter().map(|r| r.grew).sum();
        let exact: usize = tested.iter().map(|r| r.exact).sum();
        let stable = tested.iter().filter(|r| r.distinct <= 1).count();
        let ccorrect: usize = tested.iter().map(|r| r.c_correct_type).sum();
        let ctype_stable = tested.iter().filter(|r| r.c_distinct_types <= 1).count();
        let worst_j = tested
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.jacc_min.is_finite())
            .map(|r| r.jacc_min)
            .fold(1.0_f64, f64::min);
        eprintln!(
            "    S  {} faces seed-tested, {seeds} seeds: {grew} grew ({:.1}%), {exact} recovered \
             the true face set exactly ({:.1}%)",
            tested.len(),
            pct(grew, seeds),
            pct(exact, seeds),
        );
        eprintln!(
            "    S  {stable} of {} faces gave ONE outcome across all seeds; worst Jaccard vs truth \
             {worst_j:.3}",
            tested.len()
        );
        eprintln!(
            "    S  competition: {ccorrect} of {seeds} seeds picked the reference's own type \
             ({:.1}%); {ctype_stable} of {} faces agreed on a single type",
            pct(ccorrect, seeds),
            tested.len()
        );
        let od: usize = tested.iter().map(|r| r.order_diffs).sum();
        let oracle = tested.iter().filter(|r| r.oracle_same).count();
        eprintln!(
            "    G  flood traversal order changed the result on {od} of {seeds} seeds; \
             oracle-start fixpoint equals truth on {oracle} of {} faces",
            tested.len()
        );
    }
}

## 🤖💭 Assistant
<!-- msg_011Cdjpw26YdWy8jABknh527 -->

> The validation results are revealing something unexpected—a sphere is fitting a cylinder with an error of just 2.07e-7 mm, and a torus is matching two planes at 3.73e-7 mm, which directly demonstrates the super-model problem. But a sphere shouldn't be able to fit a full 32-facet cylinder at all, so something seems off here.
> 
> Actually, wait—I'm realizing the geometry works out. If the cylinder is represented as 32 quads arranged in a single row around the circumference, then all vertices lie on just two circles at different heights. Two circles of radius r at z=0 and z=h can indeed lie on a sphere centered at (0, 0, h/2) with radius √(r² + h²/4). That's why the sphere validates—the cylinder geometry actually does fit a sphere perfectly.
> 
> This is exactly the user's core problem: both the cylinder and sphere fit at machine precision because of this structural degeneracy. The residual comparison can't distinguish between them. And looking at the plane faces, the cylinder fitter returns NaN but the torus fitter gives 3.73e-7—which suggests a torus can fit a planar region too, likely because of how the cap geometry is structured.
> 
> Now I'm investigating why the rounded_cube_fine run is slow. The bottleneck seems to be in the label_faces operation combined with the competition logic—each seed runs a full 4-type grow across thousands of faces, and with 26 reference faces and 24 seeds that's hundreds of competitions to evaluate.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Invariant harness: run `--invariant-report` over every corpus model that has
# a reference STEP, and concatenate the per-reference-face TSV rows.
#
# Reuses tools/sweep.sh's model/reference pairing (`--list`) so the two
# instruments always measure the same corpus.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/invariants.sh [--out FILE] [--jobs N] [--filter REGEX] [--timeout SECS]
#                       [--seeds N] [--no-compete]
#
# Output TSV columns are documented in src/stage2/invariants.rs. Per-model
# stderr summaries go to <out>.log.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BREPPER=${BREPPER:-./target/release/brepper}
OUT=tmp/invariants.tsv
JOBS=6
FILTER=""
TIMEOUT=900
SEEDS=""
NO_COMPETE=""

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --out) OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --jobs) JOBS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --filter) FILTER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --timeout) TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --seeds) SEEDS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-compete) NO_COMPETE=1; shift ;;
        *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
LOG="$OUT.log"
: > "$LOG"

command -v gtimeout >/dev/null && TO=gtimeout || TO=timeout

run_one() {
    local model="$1" step="$2"
    local stl="tests/$model"
    local name="${model}"
    local env_args=()
    [ -n "$SEEDS" ] && env_args+=("BREPPER_INV_SEEDS=$SEEDS")
    [ -n "$NO_COMPETE" ] && env_args+=("BREPPER_INV_NO_COMPETE=1")
    local out
    out=$(env "${env_args[@]}" $TO "$TIMEOUT" "$BREPPER" "$stl" --compare "$step" \
              --stage 2.2 --invariant-report -v 2>"$LOG.$$" )
    local rc=$?
    {
        echo "=== $name (rc=$rc)"
        cat "$LOG.$$"
    } >> "$LOG"
    rm -f "$LOG.$$"
    # Rewrite the model column to the full corpus-relative stem so rows from
    # two directories with the same basename stay distinguishable.
    echo "$out" | awk -v m="${model%.stl}" -F'\t' 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} /^INV\t/ {$2=m; print}'
}

export -f run_one
export BREPPER TIMEOUT TO LOG SEEDS NO_COMPETE

# Header from a throwaway run is fragile; write it explicitly.
{
    echo "# invariants harness  seeds=${SEEDS:-default} compete=$([ -n "$NO_COMPETE" ] && echo no || echo yes)"
    printf 'kind\tmodel\tref\tsurf\tfacets\tarea\tvmax\temax\tcmax\timax\tdih_in\tdih_out\t'
    printf 'res_plane\tres_sphere\tres_cyl\tres_torus\tseeds\tgrew\texact\tdistinct\tjacc_min\t'
    printf 'over_max\tunder_max\tctypes\tccorrect\torder_diffs\toracle\tvtol\tstol\tquantum\n'
} > "$OUT"

pairs=$(./tools/sweep.sh --list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF==2 {print $1"\t"$2}')
[ -n "$FILTER" ] && pairs=$(echo "$pairs" | grep -E "$FILTER")

n=$(echo "$pairs" | grep -c .)
echo "invariants: $n model(s), jobs=$JOBS, timeout=${TIMEOUT}s" >&2

echo "$pairs" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r model step; do
    [ -z "$model" ] && continue
    echo "$model"$'\t'"$step"
done | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'IFS=$'"'"'\t'"'"' read -r m s <<< "{}"; run_one "$m" "$s"' >> "$OUT"

echo "wrote $OUT ($(grep -c '^INV' "$OUT") reference-face rows); stderr in $LOG" >&2

```

/// centroid does not have this property, which is why the initializer uses the
/// circumcenter and the diagnostic in \`crate::reference\` measures against it.
fn circumcenter(face: &MeshFace, vertices: &[MeshVertex]) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
    if (face.vertex_count as usize) < 3 {
        return None;
    }

        let mut e = [m[0][0], m[1][1], m[2][2]];
        e.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
        return e;
    }
    let q = tr / 3.0;
    let p2 = (m[0][0] - q).powi(2) + (m[1][1] - q).powi(2) + (m[2][2] - q).powi(2) + 2.0 * p1;
    let p = (p2 / 6.0).sqrt();
    let mut b = [[0.0_f64; 3]; 3];
    for i in 0..3 {
        for j in 0..3 {
            b[i][j] = (m[i][j] - if i == j { q } else { 0.0 }) / p;
        }
    }
    let det = b[0][0] * (b[1][1] * b[2][2] - b[1][2] * b[2][1])
        - b[0][1] * (b[1][0] * b[2][2] - b[1][2] * b[2][0])
        + b[0][2] * (b[1][0] * b[2][1] - b[1][1] * b[2][0]);
    let r = (det / 2.0).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
    let phi = r.acos() / 3.0;
    let e1 = q + 2.0 * p * phi.cos();
    let e3 = q + 2.0 * p * (phi + 2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI / 3.0).cos();
    let e2 = tr - e1 - e3;
    let mut e = [e1, e2, e3];
    e.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    e
}

/// Do some four of `points` lie in a plane to within `rel` of their extent?
fn any_four_coplanar(points: &[[f64; 3]], rel: f64) -> bool {
    let n = points.len();
    for i in 0..n {
        for j in (i + 1)..n {
            for k in (j + 1)..n {
                for l in (k + 1)..n {
                    let quad = [points[i], points[j], points[k], points[l]];
                    if planarity(&quad) <= rel {
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

/// Measure the section's cylinder/cone seed rule on one developable reference
/// face: every adjacent facet pair inside it is a candidate seed under
/// "a chain with exactly 6 vertices, no more than three coplanar".
fn seed_rule_probe(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    truth_axis: ([f64; 3], [f64; 3]),
) -> SeedRuleStats {
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut st = SeedRuleStats {
        pairs: 0,
        six_verts: 0,
        all_coplanar: 0,
        four_coplanar: 0,
        ax_err: Vec::new(),
        ax_err_admitted: Vec::new(),
    };
    let (_, want_dir) = truth_axis;
    let want = unit(want_dir);
    // "Coplanar" needs a scale-free bar. 1e-6 of the point set's own extent is
    // five orders below a tessellation step and is a validity floor, not a
    // tuning knob: a fused quad is coplanar to rounding, distinct rulings are
    // separated by the exporter's angular setting.
    let copl_rel = 1.0e-6;
    for &fi in faces {
        if st.pairs >= MAX_SEED_PAIRS {
            break;
        }
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let nj = ni as usize;
            if nj <= fi || !member.contains(&nj) {
                continue;
            }
            st.pairs += 1;
            let vs = vertices_of(mesh, &[fi, nj]);
            let pts: Vec<[f64; 3]> = vs.iter().map(|&v| vertex_pos(mesh, v)).collect();
            if pts.len() == 6 {
                st.six_verts += 1;
            }
            if planarity(&pts) <= copl_rel {
                st.all_coplanar += 1;
            }
            if any_four_coplanar(&pts, copl_rel) {
                st.four_coplanar += 1;
            }
            if let Some(super::initialize::Initial::Cylinder { axis_dir, .. }) =
                super::initialize::cylinder(&[fi, nj], mesh)
            {
                let d = unit(axis_dir);
                let c = [
                    d[1] * want[2] - d[2] * want[1],
                    d[2] * want[0] - d[0] * want[2],
                    d[0] * want[1] - d[1] * want[0],
                ];
                // |sin| form: linear in the error near 0, unlike acos.
                let err = norm(c).asin().to_degrees().min(
                    (180.0 - norm(c).asin().to_degrees()).abs(),
                );
                st.ax_err.push(err);
                if planarity(&pts) > copl_rel {
                    st.ax_err_admitted.push(err);
                }
            }
            if st.pairs >= MAX_SEED_PAIRS {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    st
}

fn quantile(v: &mut Vec<f64>, q: f64) -> f64 {
    if v.is_empty() {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    v.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    let i = ((v.len() - 1) as f64 * q).round() as usize;
    v[i]
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Per-reference-face measurement
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------'''

s = s.replace("                    n_adm = st.ax_err_admitted.len(),\n                );",
              "                    n_adm = st.ax_err_admitted.len(),\n                    sel = st.selected_err,\n                );")
s = s.replace('''         ax_p50\\tax_p95\\tax_max\\tn_admitted\\tadm_p50\\tadm_max"''',
              '''         ax_p50\\tax_p95\\tax_max\\tn_admitted\\tadm_p50\\tadm_max\\tselected_err"''')
s = s.replace('''            "    E  seed rule on developables: {} adjacent pairs — {} have exactly 6 vertices \\''',
              '''            "    E  seed rule on developables: {} chains (\\u{2264}4 facets) — {} have exactly 6 vertices \\''')
s = s.replace("        seedrule_worst_adm = seedrule_worst_adm.max(amax2);",
              "                seedrule_worst_adm = seedrule_worst_adm.max(amax2);\n                if st.selected_err.is_finite() {\n                    seedrule_selected_worst = seedrule_selected_worst.max(st.selected_err);\n                }")
s = s.replace("    let mut seedrule_worst_adm = 0.0_f64;",
              "    let mut seedrule_worst_adm = 0.0_f64;\n    let mut seedrule_selected_worst = 0.0_f64;")
s = s.replace('''             solvable pairs; worst {seedrule_worst_adm:.4}\\u{00b0} among the non-coplanar ones",
            seedrule_totals.4,
        );''',
'''             solvable chains; worst {seedrule_worst_adm:.4}\\u{00b0} among the non-coplanar ones — \\
             against {seedrule_selected_worst:.4}\\u{00b0} for the whole-face SELECTED pair",
            seedrule_totals.4,
        );''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Aggregate tools/invariants.sh output into the per-invariant verdicts.

Reads one or more TSV files produced by tools/invariants.sh and prints, for
each proposed invariant, how well it holds and which models break it. Nothing
here decides anything — it only summarises the measurement.
"""
import sys
import math
from collections import defaultdict

COLS = ("kind model ref surf facets area vmax emax cmax imax dih_in dih_out "
        "res_plane res_sphere res_cyl res_torus seeds grew exact distinct "
        "jacc_min over_max under_max ctypes ccorrect order_diffs oracle "
        "vtol stol quantum").split()
SR = ("kind model ref surf pairs six_verts all_coplanar four_coplanar "
      "ax_p50 ax_p95 ax_max n_admitted adm_p50 adm_max selected_err").split()


def f(x):
    try:
        return float(x)
    except Exception:
        return float("nan")


def load(paths):
    inv, sr = [], []
    for p in paths:
        for line in open(p):
            fs = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            if fs[0] == "INV" and len(fs) >= len(COLS):
                inv.append(dict(zip(COLS, fs)))
            elif fs[0] == "SEEDRULE" and len(fs) >= len(SR):
                sr.append(dict(zip(SR, fs)))
    return inv, sr


def q(vals, p):
    v = sorted(x for x in vals if not math.isnan(x))
    if not v:
        return float("nan")
    return v[min(len(v) - 1, int(round((len(v) - 1) * p)))]


def hdr(t):
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(t)
    print("=" * 78)


def main():
    inv, sr = load(sys.argv[1:])
    models = {r["model"] for r in inv}
    print(f"{len(inv)} reference faces over {len(models)} models; "
          f"{len(sr)} developable faces seed-rule-probed")

    analytic = [r for r in inv if not math.isnan(f(r["vmax"]))]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- F ----
    hdr("F. Surface Fitting Requirement — is it satisfiable on GROUND TRUTH?")
    by_t = defaultdict(list)
    for r in analytic:
        by_t[r["surf"]].append(r)
    print(f"{'type':10} {'faces':>6} {'vmax/quantum p50':>17} {'p95':>9} {'max':>10} "
          f"{'over vtol':>10}")
    for t, rs in sorted(by_t.items()):
        rel = [f(r["vmax"]) / f(r["quantum"]) for r in rs if f(r["quantum"]) > 0]
        over = sum(1 for r in rs if f(r["vmax"]) > f(r["vtol"]))
        print(f"{t:10} {len(rs):6d} {q(rel,.5):17.2f} {q(rel,.95):9.2f} "
              f"{max(rel, default=float('nan')):10.1f} {over:10d}")

    print("\n  probe adequacy: whole-facet max vs the section's chosen probe")
    ratios_e, ratios_c = [], []
    for r in analytic:
        fm = max(f(r["imax"]), f(r["cmax"]), f(r["emax"]))
        if f(r["emax"]) > 0:
            ratios_e.append(fm / f(r["emax"]))
        if f(r["cmax"]) > 0:
            ratios_c.append(fm / f(r["cmax"]))
    print(f"    facet_max / edge_mid_max : p50 {q(ratios_e,.5):.4f}  p95 {q(ratios_e,.95):.4f}  "
          f"max {max(ratios_e, default=float('nan')):.4f}   (theory: <= 1.3333)")
    print(f"    facet_max / centroid     : p50 {q(ratios_c,.5):.4f}  p95 {q(ratios_c,.95):.4f}  "
          f"max {max(ratios_c, default=float('nan')):.4f}")
    bad = sorted((fm, r) for r in analytic
                 for fm in [max(f(r['imax']), f(r['cmax']), f(r['emax'])) / f(r['emax'])
                            if f(r['emax']) > 0 else 0])[-6:]
    for v, r in reversed(bad):
        if v > 4 / 3 + 1e-9:
            print(f"      over 4/3: {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']} {v:.4f}")

    print("\n  centroid probe blindness (centroid reads ~0 where the facet does not)")
    blind = [r for r in analytic
             if f(r["emax"]) > 0 and f(r["cmax"]) < 0.25 * f(r["emax"])]
    print(f"    {len(blind)} of {len(analytic)} faces have centroid < 1/4 of the edge-mid max")
    for r in blind[:5]:
        print(f"      {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']}: "
              f"centroid {f(r['cmax']):.3e} vs edge {f(r['emax']):.3e}")

    print("\n  is --surface-tolerance 0.4 mm binding?")
    over_stol = [r for r in analytic if f(r["emax"]) > f(r["stol"])]
    allsag = [f(r["emax"]) for r in analytic]
    print(f"    true worst facet sag over the corpus: {max(allsag, default=0):.4e} mm; "
          f"p50 {q(allsag,.5):.3e}, p95 {q(allsag,.95):.3e}")
    print(f"    {len(over_stol)} reference faces exceed stol on GROUND TRUTH "
          f"(a true surface its own tolerance rejects)")
    for r in over_stol[:8]:
        print(f"      {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']}: {f(r['emax']):.4e} > {f(r['stol']):.2e}")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- A ----
    hdr("A. 'All facet relative angles within angle tolerance'")
    sep = [r for r in inv if f(r["dih_out"]) >= 0 and f(r["dih_in"]) > 0]
    insep = [r for r in sep if f(r["dih_in"]) >= f(r["dih_out"])]
    print(f"  {len(insep)} of {len(sep)} reference faces have an INTERIOR dihedral >= their "
          f"smallest BOUNDARY dihedral.")
    print("  Where that holds, no angular threshold can both keep the surface together and "
          "cut it from its neighbour.")
    worst = sorted(sep, key=lambda r: -(f(r["dih_in"]) / max(f(r["dih_out"]), 1e-9)))[:8]
    for r in worst:
        print(f"    {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']:9} interior {f(r['dih_in']):7.3f}deg  "
              f"boundary {f(r['dih_out']):7.4f}deg  ratio {f(r['dih_in'])/max(f(r['dih_out']),1e-9):8.1f}x")
    over25 = [r for r in inv if f(r["dih_in"]) > 25.0]
    print(f"\n  {len(over25)} reference faces have an interior dihedral over the 25deg default "
          f"--angular-tolerance (the sharp-edge partition SPLITS these true surfaces):")
    for r in over25[:10]:
        print(f"    {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']:9} interior {f(r['dih_in']):.2f}deg "
              f"({r['facets']} facets)")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- I ----
    hdr("I. Surface Identification — does a WRONG type also explain the true support?")
    idx = {"plane": "res_plane", "sphere": "res_sphere", "cylinder": "res_cyl",
           "cone": "res_cyl", "torus": "res_torus"}
    names = {"res_plane": "plane", "res_sphere": "sphere", "res_cyl": "cyl/cone",
             "res_torus": "torus"}
    own_fail, typed = [], 0
    impostor = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    quanta = defaultdict(list)
    for r in inv:
        own = idx.get(r["surf"])
        if own is None:
            continue
        typed += 1
        vtol, qm = f(r["vtol"]), f(r["quantum"])
        if not (f(r[own]) <= vtol):
            own_fail.append(r)
        for c in ("res_plane", "res_sphere", "res_cyl", "res_torus"):
            v = f(r[c])
            if c == own or math.isnan(v):
                continue
            if v <= vtol:
                impostor[r["surf"]][names[c]] += 1
                if qm > 0:
                    quanta[(r["surf"], names[c])].append(v / qm)
    print(f"  {len(own_fail)} of {typed} reference faces are NOT explained at vtol by a fit of "
          f"their own type:")
    for r in own_fail[:10]:
        own = idx[r["surf"]]
        print(f"    {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']:9} own-type residual {f(r[own]):.3e} "
              f"({f(r[own])/max(f(r['quantum']),1e-30):.0f} q, {r['facets']} facets)")
    print("\n  wrong types that ALSO validate the true support, and how far they sit "
          "(in float32 quanta):")
    for t in sorted(impostor):
        n = sum(1 for r in inv if r["surf"] == t)
        for c, k in sorted(impostor[t].items()):
            qs = quanta[(t, c)]
            print(f"    true {t:9} also fits as {c:9}: {k:4d} of {n:4d} faces "
                  f"(residual p50 {q(qs,.5):8.2f} q, max {max(qs, default=0):8.1f} q)")
    print("\n  own-type residual, for contrast (in quanta):")
    for t in sorted(set(r["surf"] for r in inv if r["surf"] in idx)):
        qs = [f(r[idx[t]]) / f(r["quantum"]) for r in inv
              if r["surf"] == t and f(r["quantum"]) > 0 and not math.isnan(f(r[idx[t]]))]
        print(f"    {t:9}: p50 {q(qs,.5):8.2f} q  p95 {q(qs,.95):8.2f} q  max {max(qs, default=0):9.1f} q")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- S ----
    hdr("S. Surface Seed Independence")
    tested = [r for r in inv if int(r["seeds"]) > 0]
    seeds = sum(int(r["seeds"]) for r in tested)
    grew = sum(int(r["grew"]) for r in tested)
    exact = sum(int(r["exact"]) for r in tested)
    stable = [r for r in tested if int(r["distinct"]) <= 1 and int(r["grew"]) == int(r["seeds"])]
    print(f"  {len(tested)} reference faces seed-tested with {seeds} seeds")
    print(f"    seeds that grew anything          : {grew:5d} ({100*grew/max(seeds,1):.1f}%)")
    print(f"    seeds that recovered the TRUE set : {exact:5d} ({100*exact/max(seeds,1):.1f}%)")
    print(f"    faces where EVERY seed grew and all seeds agreed: {len(stable)} of {len(tested)} "
          f"({100*len(stable)/max(len(tested),1):.1f}%)")
    byt = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0, 0])
    for r in tested:
        b = byt[r["surf"]]
        b[0] += int(r["seeds"]); b[1] += int(r["grew"]); b[2] += int(r["exact"])
        b[3] += 1 if (int(r["distinct"]) <= 1 and int(r["grew"]) == int(r["seeds"])) else 0
    print(f"\n  {'type':10} {'faces':>6} {'seeds':>6} {'grew%':>7} {'exact%':>7} {'stable faces':>13}")
    for t in sorted(byt):
        s, g, e, st = byt[t]
        n = sum(1 for r in tested if r["surf"] == t)
        print(f"  {t:10} {n:6d} {s:6d} {100*g/max(s,1):7.1f} {100*e/max(s,1):7.1f} "
              f"{st:6d}/{n:<6d}")
    unstable = sorted(tested, key=lambda r: (f(r["jacc_min"]) if not math.isnan(f(r["jacc_min"])) else 2))
    print("\n  worst seed-dependence (lowest Jaccard of a grown set vs the truth):")
    for r in unstable[:12]:
        if math.isnan(f(r["jacc_min"])):
            continue
        print(f"    {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']:9} {r['facets']:>6} facets: "
              f"{r['grew']}/{r['seeds']} grew, {r['exact']} exact, {r['distinct']} distinct, "
              f"jacc {f(r['jacc_min']):.3f}, leak-out {100*f(r['over_max']):.0f}%, "
              f"stop-short {100*f(r['under_max']):.0f}%")
    leaks = [r for r in tested if f(r["over_max"]) > 0.02]
    shorts = [r for r in tested if f(r["under_max"]) > 0.02]
    print(f"\n  {len(leaks)} faces where some seed leaked >2% of its set ACROSS a true boundary")
    print(f"  {len(shorts)} faces where some seed stopped >2% short of the true surface")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- G ----
    hdr("G. Growth Independence")
    od = sum(int(r["order_diffs"]) for r in tested)
    orc = sum(1 for r in tested if r["oracle"] == "1")
    print(f"  reversing the flood's neighbour order changed the result on {od} of {seeds} seeds")
    print(f"  starting the refit fixpoint from the WHOLE true face set reproduces the truth on "
          f"{orc} of {len(tested)} faces ({100*orc/max(len(tested),1):.1f}%)")
    disagree = [r for r in tested
                if (r["oracle"] == "1") != (int(r["exact"]) == int(r["seeds"]) and int(r["seeds"]) > 0)]
    print(f"  {len(disagree)} faces where the oracle start and the seed starts disagree "
          f"(the fixpoint is start-dependent):")
    for r in disagree[:10]:
        print(f"    {r['model']}#{r['ref']} {r['surf']:9} oracle={r['oracle']} "
              f"seeds exact {r['exact']}/{r['seeds']}")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- E ----
    hdr("E. Surface Seed Requirements (the stated cylinder/cone seed rule)")
    if sr:
        tot = sum(int(x["pairs"]) for x in sr)
        six = sum(int(x["six_verts"]) for x in sr)
        allc = sum(int(x["all_coplanar"]) for x in sr)
        four = sum(int(x["four_coplanar"]) for x in sr)
        print(f"  {len(sr)} developable reference faces, {tot} facet chains (<=4 facets) enumerated")
        print(f"    with exactly 6 distinct vertices        : {six} ({100*six/max(tot,1):.1f}%)")
        print(f"    of those, ALL SIX coplanar (degenerate) : {allc} ({100*allc/max(six,1):.2f}%)")
        print(f"    of those, SOME FOUR coplanar            : {four} ({100*four/max(six,1):.2f}%)")
        print("    -> read literally, 'no more than three coplanar' rejects that last group.")
        amax = [f(x["ax_max"]) for x in sr]
        sel = [f(x["selected_err"]) for x in sr]
        print(f"\n  closed-form axis error from a bare 6-vertex chain: "
              f"p50 {q(amax,.5):.4f}deg p95 {q(amax,.95):.4f}deg max {max(amax, default=0):.4f}deg")
        print(f"  same, from the whole face with Phase-1.1 pair SELECTION: "
              f"p50 {q(sel,.5):.4f}deg p95 {q(sel,.95):.4f}deg max {max(sel, default=0):.4f}deg")
        worst = sorted(sr, key=lambda x: -f(x["ax_max"]))[:8]
        print("\n  worst bare-chain axis errors:")
        for x in worst:
            print(f"    {x['model']}#{x['ref']} {x['surf']:9} chain max {f(x['ax_max']):9.4f}deg  "
                  f"selected {f(x['selected_err']):9.4f}deg  ({x['six_verts']} chains)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<summary>Tool Result</summary>

```
/// Deterministic single pass: a purely local dihedral-angle test.
pub fn classify_edges(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, angular_tolerance: f64) -> EdgeClassification {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let centroids: Vec<[f64; 3]> = mesh
        .faces
        .iter()
        .map(|f| face_centroid(f, &mesh.vertices))
        .collect();

    let mut class = vec![[EdgeClass::Interior; 4]; n];
    let mut kappa = vec![[f64::NAN; 4]; n];
    let (mut sharp_count, mut interior_count) = (0, 0);
    for fi in 0..n {
        let Some(n1) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else { continue };
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for e in 0..vc {
            let ni = mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[e];
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            let Some(n2) = mesh.faces[ni].normal else { continue };
            let th = dot3(&n1, &n2).clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos();
            let dx = centroids[ni][0] - centroids[fi][0];
            let dy = centroids[ni][1] - centroids[fi][1];
            let dz = centroids[ni][2] - centroids[fi][2];
            let d = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
            if d <= 1e-12 {
                continue;
            }
            let below = n1[0] * dx + n1[1] * dy + n1[2] * dz <= 0.0;
            kappa[fi][e] = if below { th / d } else { -th / d };
            if th > angular_tolerance {
                class[fi][e] = EdgeClass::Sharp;
            }
            if fi < ni {
                match class[fi][e] {
                    EdgeClass::Sharp => sharp_count += 1,
                    EdgeClass::Interior => interior_count += 1,
                }
            }
        }
    }

    EdgeClassification {
        class,
        kappa,
        sharp_count,
        interior_count,
    }
}
```
</details>

> Let me double-check a couple of key measurements before finalizing: confirming that `simple_cylinder`'s sphere impostor represents the 2-ring degeneracy by looking at distinct axial levels, and verifying the 9/4 centroid bound holds (measured max of 2.2391 against the theoretical 2.25). I'll wait for the final data to lock in the exact numbers I'll cite.
> 
> Drafting the report structure now...
> 
> Three of the five main headings hold up under measurement, but two need significant reframing, and several specific claims are contradicted by the data. Growth Independence checks out cleanly with zero violations. Surface Fitting is achievable but the probe approach is flawed in a correctable way, and the three variants actually collapse into one. Surface Identification reveals the core issue—the tie-break using residual magnitude fails almost entirely, pointing the wrong direction 99% of the time. Seed Requirements exposes a major problem: the coplanarity constraint rejects three-quarters of valid seeds while catching none of the invalid ones, and even rule-conforming chains can produce axes off by 90 degrees. Seed Independence is substantially broken today, affecting over a third of surfaces, and fixing it requires a precondition that turns out to be vacuous on most cases.
> 
> Beyond the measurement failures, the text itself has issues—truncated sentences, contradictory definitions, typos, and unresolved thresholds marked as TBD that the existing ladder already answers implicitly.
> 
> The core recommendation is consolidating the three per-type fitting rules into a single unified rule: all vertices stay within vertex tolerance, and all edge midpoints of the triangulated facet (including boundary edges and quad diagonals) stay within three-quarters of the surface tolerance. This gives a rigorous second-order bound across the whole facet and resolves both open questions. The measured performance shows this is tighter than the current boundary-only or centroid approaches.
> 
> The second recommendation is to express tolerances in the actual units of the data—vertex tolerance as float32 position quantization units, and surface tolerance as a multiple of the facet's local sag. This grounds the abstract thresholds in something measurable and concrete.
> 
> For the third point, angular tolerance shouldn't be used as a membership test, and it needs to be raised. Most faces have interior dihedral angles that exceed the smallest boundary dihedral, which means the current angular tolerance is already cutting through true surfaces on hundreds of edges. The worst cases come from exporters like Fusion using loose presets like 30° against a 25° default. The fix is to require the angular tolerance to be at least as large as what the exporter itself announces, which recovers the right threshold on curvature-dominated meshes, though the current repair stage undoes some of this work.
> 
> For the fourth point, I need to remove the coplanarity requirement from the seed rule and replace the rigid "exactly 6 vertices" constraint with a selection from a larger pool. The data shows that nearly three-quarters of 6-vertex chains have at least four coplanar vertices, so the strict rule rejects most of them, yet removing the wholly-coplanar ones doesn't improve the worst-case axis error. Selecting from the full face pool gives much better results—p95 error of 0.33° for cylinders versus 3.14° for a bare chain, and for cones the bare-chain median error jumps to 46°.
> 
> The identification invariant needs an identifiability precondition, and the residual metric can't answer the "how do we choose" question that's still open.
> 
> For the sixth point, I'm redefining Seed Independence as a closure property of the output itself rather than a quantifier over different seeds. I'll define admissible surfaces as those where the surface is connected, the fit is optimal for that surface, every facet validates, and no adjacent facet validates. This becomes checkable in linear time on the output, and seed independence shifts to mean the algorithm finds all admissible surfaces and the selection among them depends only on the set, not the order—making the invariant testable per run instead of requiring re-runs.
> 
> I also need to add two missing invariants: the partition invariant stating every facet belongs to exactly one surface (already enforced but not explicitly stated), and a boundary invariant. There's also a seam-group issue with the reference facet that's worth noting.

> I'm also being careful about the instrument's own limitations—the ground truth comes from the `--compare` reference, but about a third of the wild pairs aren't recorded ground truth and carry tail artifacts. The `cone_15x20.step` is a faceted reference, seeds are sampled at 8-12 per face rather than exhaustively, freeform reference faces lack closed-form distance measurements, and the current `grow` algorithm is a blind-patch approach, so the seed-independence numbers reflect today's implementation rather than a theoretical bound.
