I read DEVELOPMENT_PLAN, README, TODO and your new Invariants section, built the measuring instrument, and ran it over the corpus. Nothing in the invariants or the algorithm was changed.

## Verdict on the new material

**The framing is right and worth building on.** "Define near-invariants first, then make the algorithm satisfy them" is the correct move for this codebase, and two of your five headings turn out to be *provable* rather than merely empirical — which is better than you hoped. But the section as written has one truncated sentence, one self-contradictory definition, and three specifics that measurement refutes outright. It is not workable as-is; it is workable after edits I can enumerate precisely.

## What I built

- **`--invariant-report`** (`src/stage2/invariants.rs`, ~1400 lines) — runs after stage 2.2, needs `--compare`. It reuses `reference::label_faces`, which already labels every mesh facet with its ground-truth reference face for free, so each proposed invariant is scored against the reference's *own exact* surface parameters.
- **`tools/invariants.sh`** — harness over `sweep.sh`'s model/reference pairing; **`tools/inv_analyze.py`** — aggregator.
- One production refactor: extracted `compete_from_seed` verbatim out of `compete_region` so the harness drives the *real* competition rather than a reimplementation. Suite **595 passed / 0 failed**, clippy clean, `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine` still 26 = 6/12/8.

Coverage: **147 models, 2303 reference faces, 10 128 seed runs, 179 414 candidate seed chains**; a deep pass with the full four-type competition per seed over 103 models / 7630 seeds.

Instrument sanity check: it independently reproduced Phase 1.0's recorded **1.0342°** adjacent-pair cylinder-axis error on `pipe_elbow_10` medium.

---

## Findings

### 1. Fitting Requirement — satisfiable, but the probes are wrong (fixably)

Your three per-type probe rules collapse into **one** rule with a proof behind it. For a facet with vertices on the surface, the deviation is a quadratic vanishing at the vertices, so in barycentrics `e = −Σλᵢλⱼ·qᵢⱼ`. The max over the facet is therefore between the largest **edge-midpoint** value and 4/3 of it, exactly, to second order. Measured over 895 non-degenerate faces:

| probe | p95 ratio to true facet max | max |
|---|---|---|
| boundary edge midpoints (as written) | 1.742 | 1.999 |
| edge midpoints **+ quad diagonals** | **1.012** | **1.497** |
| facet centroid | 1.384 | 2.239 |

The centroid's 2.239 matches the derived worst case of 9/4 to three digits, and on a saddle the centroid can read exactly zero where the facet is off by the full sag. **The centroid is not a bound on anything.** The boundary-only version fails at exactly 2.0 on quad-tessellated spheres because a parallelogram's diagonal midpoint *is* its centre, where the sag is 2× the side midpoints'.

So: edge midpoints of a *triangulation* (boundary edges plus fused-quad diagonals), times 4/3, is a rigorous whole-facet bound at ~1.5 distance evaluations per triangle. That answers both of your TODOs — including the NURBS one — with one rule instead of three.

**Vertex tolerance.** On verified synthetic ground truth the invariant holds at p95 ≈ 1.5 float32 quanta, max ≈ 5. But two true cylinders on `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets_fine` sit at **8.8 and 8.5 quanta = 7.7e-5 mm, over the 5e-5 default vtol**. The requirement is *unsatisfiable* there today — no algorithm can recover those two surfaces.

**Surface tolerance.** True facet sag over the corpus spans p50 2.2e-6 to max 0.325 mm — five orders of magnitude — against a single 0.4 mm default with 1.23× margin at the worst point. This is your Phase 3.2 per-face-tolerance argument arriving from the invariant side.

### 2. "All facet relative angles within angle tolerance" — refuted as a membership rule

**856 of 1073 reference faces have an interior dihedral ≥ their smallest boundary dihedral.** Worst: `nosecone_medium`'s sphere, 17.58° inside vs 0.021° across the tangency — 822×. No threshold separates those.

Worse, it is already doing damage as a *partition* rule: stage 2.1's own classifier calls **350 edges sharp strictly inside 68 true reference surfaces**, cutting them before any fitting. `filleted_pipe` gets 11 sharp edges inside each of its two big tori (interior dihedral 31.4°); stage 2.4's repair silently sews them back. That is precisely the heuristic-on-heuristic you want gone. The largest cluster is Fusion's coarse preset — **30° normal deviation against a 25° default angular tolerance**, so every coarse Fusion cylinder is cut into 12 pieces.

### 3. Surface Identification — your proposed tie-break points the wrong way

The TODO asks how to choose when a cone also fits a cylinder. Measured, on the true support of each reference face:

| true type | a wrong type also validates at vtol |
|---|---|
| cylinder | sphere on **496 of 652**; torus on 307 |
| cone | sphere on 64 of 91; torus on 32 |
| plane | sphere on 322 of 1261; cyl/cone on 126 |

And the residuals are indistinguishable — both sit at ~0.2–0.5 quanta. The decisive number:

> **On 393 of 397 true cylinders (99%), the impostor sphere fits the cylinder's own facets *better* than the cylinder does** (median 0.555× the residual, p95 0.991).

So "the cylindrical fit should fit much more precisely" is not merely a weak signal — it is systematically **inverted**. `simple_cylinder` shows why cleanly: its 32-quad band has vertices on exactly two circles, which lie exactly on a sphere; residual 2.07e-7 mm, machine precision. This is identifiability, not model selection, and it is the same wall your DEVELOPMENT_PLAN already documents under `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`.

### 4. Surface Seed Independence — badly false today

Running the production `grow` from seeds spread across each true surface:

| type | faces | seeds | grew | recovered truth | faces where all seeds agreed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plane | 326 | 2569 | 93.1% | 91.5% | 284/326 (87%) |
| sphere | 139 | 1112 | 70.7% | 64.5% | 21/139 (15%) |
| torus | 129 | 1030 | 68.3% | 18.3% | **2/129 (2%)** |
| cylinder | 612 | 4785 | 56.7% | 48.3% | 133/612 (22%) |
| cone | 79 | 632 | 28.2% | 24.8% | 8/79 (10%) |
| **all** | **1285** | **10128** | **66.8%** | **56.5%** | **448/1285 (34.9%)** |

Failure *direction* differs by type and matches the recorded history: cones **never leak** and starve (0% leak, 11% stop-short — the Phase 1.2 chicken-and-egg); tori and spheres both leak and starve (~40–53% each). Seam-split reference faces account for almost none of it (union scoring moves 56.5% → 58.3%).

Restricting to **interior** seeds (every mesh neighbour in the same reference face) helps a lot — grew 66.8% → 87.5%, agreeing faces 34.9% → 63.8% — but **74% of reference faces have no interior facet at all** (median 29 facets; strip-tessellated cylinders are one quad row, so every facet touches a cap). An interiority precondition would be vacuous where it is most needed.

At the **type** level the picture is much better. Full competition per seed: 91.9% of faces had every seed agree on one winning type, and conditional on producing a winner — cyl 95%, plane 98%, sphere 90%, torus 96%, cone 85% correct. **The type is nearly seed-independent; the extent is not.**

### 5. Growth Independence — provable, and confirmed

`flood` is defined as the connected component of `{faces validating a fixed fit}` containing the seed, returned sorted. That is a set, so it is order-independent by construction. Re-running every flood with the neighbour iteration reversed: **0 differences in 18 429 seeds.**

The real order dependence is the *refit fixpoint* `F ← flood(fit(F))`. Starting it from the whole true face set instead of the seed patch reproduces the truth on only 83.0%, and **648 of 1285 faces disagree between the oracle start and the seed starts**. So state this heading as a theorem about `flood` and put the empirical burden on the fixpoint.

### 6. Seed Requirements — the stated cylinder/cone rule is unusable as written

Enumerating every ≤4-facet chain inside each developable reference face:

- 14.2% have exactly 6 distinct vertices.
- **74.5% of those have some four coplanar** — a fused quad is coplanar by construction, so read literally, *"no more than three of which are coplanar" rejects three-quarters of the valid seeds*, including the best ones.
- Only 4.4% are wholly coplanar (the degeneracy you're actually aiming at), **and excluding them does not lower the worst axis error at all** — 90° either way.
- Axis error from a rule-conforming chain: p50 0.0000° but **p95 21.8°, max 90°**. For cones the per-face median is **46°**, and 76 of 87 cone faces have a conforming chain more than 1° wrong. (Phase 1.1 already recorded why: a real cone tessellation is a single ring, and every normal line meets the axis at the same point.)
- The same initializer over the **whole face with Phase 1.1's pair selection**: p95 **0.10°**, max 3.07° on synthetic ground truth. ~200× better.

Counting vertices is the wrong shape of condition. What makes a seed good is having enough facets to *select* a ruling-aligned, angularly-distant pair from.

### 7. Textual defects

- "Surfaces can be discovered by growing a set of seed facets to the set of contiguous facets that satisfy " — sentence truncated.
- "A **non-contiguous** facet chain is a set of facets where each facet shares a single edge with **any** other facet" — self-contradictory; that definition is *contiguous*, and "any" should be "some". Also "non-contiuous" typo twice.
- "Fitted cylinder must not have such a large radius as to be effectively planar. (TBD!)" is a new tuned threshold, which TODO rule 5 says needs sign-off — and the ladder's simplest-DOF-first rule already answers it without one.

---

## Recommendations (not implemented)

1. **Collapse the three fitting rules into one**: all vertices ≤ vtol; all edge midpoints of a facet *triangulation* (boundary edges + fused-quad diagonals) ≤ ¾·stol. Drop facet centroids entirely — they are not a bound. This covers NURBS too and answers both TODOs.
2. **State tolerances in the units the data has**: vertex bar in float32 position bounds (~2 quanta p95, ~5 max), surface bar as a multiple of the facet's own local sag. A global 5e-5 makes two true `stepped_block` cylinders unrecoverable by construction.
3. **Demote the angular condition** from a membership/partition rule to a post-hoc consistency check, and require the angular tolerance to exceed the exporter's own angular setting (Fusion Low is 30° > the 25° default). Today 68 true surfaces are cut and repaired back.
4. **Rewrite the seed rule as a selection over a pool, not a minimal set.** Delete the coplanarity clause (it rejects 74.5% of good seeds and catches none of the bad). Keep a rank/conditioning condition instead — Phase 1.1's `select_axis_pair` already is it.
5. **Add an identifiability precondition to Surface Identification**, and record in the section that the residual-magnitude tie-break is measured-dead (99% inverted). The discriminator has to stay structural: ladder order plus `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`-style tests.
6. **Restate Seed Independence declaratively, as a property of the output.** Call `(T, θ, F)` *admissible* iff `F` is mesh-connected, `θ = fit_T(F)`, every facet of `F` validates `θ`, and no facet adjacent to `F` does. That is checkable in O(|F|) on every run, it makes Growth Independence a corollary rather than an experiment, and it converts an unbounded for-all-over-seeds into a finite check. Seed independence then becomes "the admissible set is small and the algorithm finds all of it".
7. **Add the two missing invariants**: the partition invariant (every facet in exactly one surface — `assert_invariants` enforces it, but the section doesn't state it), and a *boundary* invariant, since every current statement is per-surface and the junction rows are where the difficulty actually lives.

## Caveats on the measurement

Ground truth is the `--compare` reference, and roughly a third of the wild `external/` pairs are recorded as not-ground-truth — the vertex-invariant tails (1313 quanta) come from there; the synthetic split is in the report. `cone_15x20.step` is a faceted 59-plane reference, and its rows show up as degenerate 1-facet "planes". Freeform reference faces are unmeasured (no closed-form distance). Seeds are sampled 8–12 per face, not exhaustive. And the seed-independence numbers describe *today's* blind-patch `grow` — they are a baseline, not a bound on what's achievable.

Full output: `tmp/inv-report-broad.txt`, `tmp/inv-report-deep.txt`, raw TSVs in `tmp/inv-{broad,deep}.tsv`. Nothing is committed — the working tree has the tool plus your two doc edits.

```
fn chains_with_six_vertices(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    member: &HashSet<usize>,
    cap: usize,
) -> (Vec<Vec<usize>>, usize) {
    let mut out: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
    let mut considered = 0usize;
    for &start in faces {
        if out.len() >= cap {
            break;
        }
        // Depth-first enumeration of simple paths from \`start\`.
        let mut stack: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![vec![start]];
        while let Some(path) = stack.pop() {
            if out.len() >= cap {
                break;
            }
            if path.len() >= 2 {
                considered += 1;
                if vertices_of(mesh, &path).len() == 6 {
                    let mut p = path.clone();
                    p.sort_unstable();
                    out.push(p);
                }
            }
            if path.len() >= MAX_CHAIN {
                continue;
            }
            let last = *path.last().unwrap();
            let vc = mesh.faces[last].vertex_count as usize;
            for &ni in &mesh.faces[last].neighbors[..vc] {
                if ni < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let nj = ni as usize;
                if !member.contains(&nj) || path.contains(&nj) {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut next = path.clone();
                next.push(nj);
                stack.push(next);
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort();
    out.dedup();
    (out, considered)
}
```

```bash
/// deduplicating its numerator by face set, and it mixes chain lengths 2/3/4
/// when only one length can reach 6 vertices for a given facet shape.
fn chain_dump(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    member: &HashSet<usize>,
    model: &str,
    r: usize,
    kind: &str,
) {
    // (chain length, quad count in chain) -> vertex-count histogram
    let mut seen: HashSet<Vec<usize>> = HashSet::new();
    let mut hist: std::collections::BTreeMap<(usize, usize, usize), usize> =
        std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    let mut stack: Vec<Vec<usize>> = faces.iter().map(|&f| vec![f]).collect();
    let mut budget = 200_000usize;
    while let Some(path) = stack.pop() {
        if budget == 0 {
            break;
        }
        budget -= 1;
        if path.len() >= 2 {
            let mut key = path.clone();
            key.sort_unstable();
            if seen.insert(key) {
                let quads = path
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|&&f| mesh.faces[f].vertex_count == 4)
                    .count();
                let nv = vertices_of(mesh, &path).len();
                *hist.entry((path.len(), quads, nv)).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
        if path.len() >= MAX_CHAIN {
            continue;
        }
        let last = *path.last().unwrap();
        let vc = mesh.faces[last].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[last].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let nj = ni as usize;
            if member.contains(&nj) && !path.contains(&nj) {
                let mut next = path.clone();
                next.push(nj);
                stack.push(next);
            }
        }
    }
    for ((len, quads, nv), n) in hist {
        println!("CHAIN\\t{model}\\t{r}\\t{kind}\\t{len}\\t{quads}\\t{nv}\\t{n}");
    }
}"""
```

```
pub(crate) fn min_ruling_gap_rad(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    fi: usize,
    axis_pos: [f64; 3],
    axis_dir: [f64; 3],
) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut d = axis_dir;
    if normalize3(&mut d) == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);

    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
    if n < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut thetas = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    for k in 0..n {
        let vtx = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        let w = [
            vtx.x - axis_pos[0],
            vtx.y - axis_pos[1],
            vtx.z - axis_pos[2],
        ];
        let axial = dot3(&w, &d);
        let radial = [
            w[0] - axial * d[0],
            w[1] - axial * d[1],
            w[2] - axial * d[2],
        ];
        thetas.push(dot3(&radial, &v).atan2(dot3(&radial, &u)));
    }

    let mut min_gap = f64::MAX;
    for i in 0..n {
        for j in (i + 1)..n {
            let mut delta = (thetas[i] - thetas[j]).abs();
            if delta > std::f64::consts::PI {
                delta = std::f64::consts::TAU - delta;
            }
            min_gap = min_gap.min(delta);
        }
    }
    Some(min_gap)
}

/// \`|n_i × n_j|\` — how well-conditioned the pair is as an axis source, and
/// exactly the denominator in the amplification law.
fn pair_conditioning(a: &[f64; 3], b: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    let c = cross3(a, b);
    (c[0] * c[0] + c[1] * c[1] + c[2] * c[2]).sqrt()
}

/// The most angularly distant pair of facet normals in \`faces\`.
fn widest_normal_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, f64)> {
    let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, f64)> = None;
    for (a, &fi) in faces.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(ni) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        for &fj in &faces[a + 1..] {
            let Some(nj) = mesh.faces[fj].normal else {
                continue;
            };
            let k = pair_conditioning(&ni, &nj);
            if best.is_none_or(|(_, _, bk)| k > bk) {
                best = Some((fi, fj, k));
            }
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Pick the pair of facets to take an axis from: ruling-aligned, and as
/// angularly distant as the patch allows.
///
/// Two passes, because alignment is defined relative to an axis we do not have
/// yet. The first pass gives a provisional axis good enough to *classify*
/// facets — misjudging alignment needs an axis error of order the angular step,
/// far beyond what pass one produces — and the second pass re-picks among the
/// facets that survive. If too few survive, the provisional pair stands: a
/// worse-conditioned axis is still better than no axis, and validation
/// downstream is what decides whether the fit lives.
///
/// Returns the pair and the axis direction it implies.
fn select_axis_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, [f64; 3])> {
    let axis_of = |fi: usize, fj: usize| -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        let (ni, nj) = (mesh.faces[fi].normal?, mesh.faces[fj].normal?);
        let mut axis = cross3(&ni, &nj);
        if normalize3(&mut axis) < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
            return None;
        }
        Some(axis)
    };

    let (pi, pj, _) = widest_normal_pair(faces, mesh)?;
    let provisional = axis_of(pi, pj)?;

    // Any point on the provisional axis will do to measure ruling gaps: the
    // gap is an angle about the axis direction, and shifting the reference
    // point along or across the axis moves every vertex's θ together.
    let anchor = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[pi], &mesh.vertices);
    let aligned: Vec<usize> = faces
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|&fi| {
            min_ruling_gap_rad(mesh, fi, anchor, provisional)
                .is_some_and(|gap| gap < RULING_SAME_RAD)
        })
        .collect();

    if aligned.len() >= 2 {
        if let Some((ai, aj, _)) = widest_normal_pair(&aligned, mesh) {
            if let Some(axis) = axis_of(ai, aj) {
                return Some((ai, aj, axis));
            }
        }
    }
    Some((pi, pj, provisional))
}

/// Every distinct vertex index used by \`faces\`.
fn patch_vertices(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &fi in faces {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let vi = f.vertex_indices[k];
            if !out.contains(&vi) {
                out.push(vi);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```bash
fn sym4_eigenvalues(m0: &[[f64; 4]; 4]) -> [f64; 4] {
    let mut a = *m0;
    for _ in 0..24 {
        let mut off = 0.0_f64;
        for i in 0..4 {
            for j in (i + 1)..4 {
                off += a[i][j] * a[i][j];
            }
        }
        if off <= 1e-30 {
            break;
        }
        for p in 0..3 {
            for q in (p + 1)..4 {
                if a[p][q].abs() <= 1e-300 {
                    continue;
                }
                let theta = (a[q][q] - a[p][p]) / (2.0 * a[p][q]);
                let t = theta.signum() / (theta.abs() + (theta * theta + 1.0).sqrt());
                let c = 1.0 / (t * t + 1.0).sqrt();
                let s = t * c;
                let mut b = a;
                for k in 0..4 {
                    b[p][k] = c * a[p][k] - s * a[q][k];
                    b[q][k] = s * a[p][k] + c * a[q][k];
                }
                let mut d = b;
                for k in 0..4 {
                    d[k][p] = c * b[k][p] - s * b[k][q];
                    d[k][q] = s * b[k][p] + c * b[k][q];
                }
                a = d;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut e = [a[0][0], a[1][1], a[2][2], a[3][3]];
    e.sort_by(|x, y| x.partial_cmp(y).unwrap());
    e
}

/// The **dual** (plane-coordinate) view of a developable seed.
///
/// Every facet plane of a cone contains the apex (Phase 1.1), and every facet
/// plane of a cylinder is parallel to the axis — the same statement in
/// homogeneous coordinates. Writing facet `i`'s plane as the 4-vector
/// `(nᵢ, −nᵢ·pᵢ)`, a cone with apex `A` makes every plane orthogonal to
/// `(A, 1)` and a cylinder with axis direction `u` makes every plane orthogonal
/// to `(u, 0)`. So for ANY developable of revolution the facet planes span a
/// 3-dimensional subspace of ℝ⁴, and the apex-or-axis **is the null vector** —
/// with `w₄ ≠ 0` reading as a cone at `w₁₂₃/w₄` and `w₄ = 0` as a cylinder
/// along `w₁₂₃`, continuously, no infinity in between.
///
/// That makes the two singular-value ratios below the natural statement of what
/// a seed has to satisfy, in place of counting vertices:
///
/// - `sigma4` (smallest / largest) — how *developable* the patch is. Non-zero
///   means the facets do not lie on any common cone or cylinder.
/// - `sigma3` (second-smallest / largest) — whether the patch **identifies**
///   one. Zero means the null space is 2-dimensional, i.e. the apex is a free
///   point on a line and a cylinder is indistinguishable from a one-parameter
///   family of cones. A triangle fan around a shared vertex on a cylinder is
///   exactly this case, and so is a patch confined to a single ruling.
///
/// Coordinates are shifted to the patch centroid and scaled by its extent
/// first: the `n` block is dimensionless and the `−n·p` block carries length,
/// so without normalization the spectrum measures the choice of origin rather
/// than the data (the same trap Phase 1.1 hit with the torus Plücker system).
fn plane_spectrum(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
    if faces.len() < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut c = [0.0_f64; 3];
    let mut cnt = 0.0_f64;
    for &fi in faces {
        let q = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        for k in 0..3 {
            c[k] += q[k];
        }
        cnt += 1.0;
    }
    for k in 0..3 {
        c[k] /= cnt;
    }
    let mut extent = 0.0_f64;
    for &fi in faces {
        for p in facet_points(mesh, fi) {
            extent = extent.max(norm(sub(p, c)));
        }
    }
    if extent <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut g = [[0.0_f64; 4]; 4];
    for &fi in faces {
        let n = facet_normal(mesh, fi);
        let p = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        let pt = [
            (p[0] - c[0]) / extent,
            (p[1] - c[1]) / extent,
            (p[2] - c[2]) / extent,
        ];
        let v = [n[0], n[1], n[2], -dot(n, pt)];
        for i in 0..4 {
            for j in 0..4 {
                g[i][j] += v[i] * v[j];
            }
        }
    }
    let e = sym4_eigenvalues(&g);
    if e[3] <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    // Singular values are sqrt of the Gram's eigenvalues.
    Some((
        (e[0].max(0.0) / e[3]).sqrt(),
        (e[1].max(0.0) / e[3]).sqrt(),
    ))
}

/// Do all the facets of `chain` share one common vertex? (The case the
/// Invariants section's coplanarity clause was reaching for.)
fn shares_common_vertex(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, chain: &[usize]) -> bool {
    let mut common: Option<HashSet<usize>> = None;
    for &fi in chain {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        let set: HashSet<usize> = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied().collect();
        common = Some(match common {
            None => set,
            Some(c) => c.intersection(&set).copied().collect(),
        });
        if common.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.is_empty()) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    common.is_some_and(|c| !c.is_empty())
}
```

> The real insight is that cone failures aren't a seed-quality issue at all — they stem from the fundamental structural degeneracy already identified: a cone tessellation is inherently a single ring, and a short chain of three to four facets on it cannot determine the axis because all the normal lines converge at the apex and all facet planes contain it, leaving the apex locally under-determined. This 45.6° median error represents missing information, not poor conditioning. The distinction matters: what's being excluded isn't a combinatorial configuration but rather the absence of the observable that would pin down the parameter. Over **27 984 six-vertex chains on 107 models**, 9 587 (34.3%) produce an axis more than 1° wrong. Scored as detectors of exactly those:

Making your intent literal doesn't help — on these meshes "shares a vertex" and "some four coplanar" are nearly the same predicate, and both throw away five good seeds for every bad one they catch.

**My own proposal was worse, and I should report it as dead.** The idea was that a cone's facet planes all contain the apex and a cylinder's are all parallel to the axis, so in homogeneous coordinates `(nᵢ, −nᵢ·pᵢ)` both are one statement — the planes span a 3-space and the apex-or-axis *is* the null vector, with `w₄ → 0` sliding continuously from cone to cylinder. It is elegant and it does not work. Measured on its own terms, the null-vector axis is worse than `n₁ × n₂` at every facet count (k=2: p50 14.8° vs 0.0000°), cone apexes land 4.8–8.6× the patch extent away at the median, and `w₄` does not separate cylinders from cones at all (true cylinders p50 0.41, true cones p50 0.71, ranges overlapping). It's the "detector needs just one threshold" trap from a new direction.

## Why none of them works

The measurement says the thing you're excluding isn't a property of the facet set's combinatorics. It's **per-parameter identifiability, and one seed can pin one parameter while leaving another free.** Same corpus:

- **Cylinder axis** — ruling alignment governs it, exactly as Phase 1.0 predicted. With ≥2 aligned facets and `|n₁×n₂| ≥ 1e-3`: p50 **0.0000°**, p95 1.76°. Otherwise: p50 0.118°, p95 3.22°.
- **Cylinder radius** — a *different* observable, and mostly absent: **87% of these chains sweep under 20° about their own axis**, so the radius is undetermined even where the axis is exact. That is precisely `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`'s quantity, already in `compete.rs` and already measured essential.
- **Cone apex and half-angle** — nothing local determines them. Axis error is p50 **45.6°** regardless of alignment, regardless of coplanarity, and regardless of axial span (I checked: 0 of 8 128 cone chains are the degenerate single ring, so that isn't the cause either). The same initializer over the **whole face** reads p50 0.0006°, with 70 of 91 cone faces under 0.01° — `simple_cone` 0.0021°, `cone_cylinder` 0.0053°, `nosecone` 0.0135°.

And your fan *is* genuinely degenerate — just not for the reason you gave. Every 2-facet chain shares a vertex and reads dual-rank 2 (σ₃ p50 9.1e-14), so the apex really is a free point on a line. But its cylinder axis is exact anyway (p50 0.0000°, p95 0.0002°). The degeneracy is in the **apex**, not the axis.

## A better way to express it

Drop the per-type seed rules and state a condition on the *support* instead:

> **Seed admissibility.** A candidate (type, support) is admissible only where the support determines every parameter of that type. Each clause names its observable, not a facet count:
>
> - **axis direction** (cylinder, cone, torus) — at least two facets that are ruling-aligned about the candidate axis, with `|n₁ × n₂|` above the numeric conditioning floor. *(Measured: takes the cylinder axis p95 from 3.22° to 1.76° and the median to exactly 0.)*
> - **radius** (cylinder, sphere, torus major) — the support must sweep about the axis. *(This is `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`; no new constant.)*
> - **apex and half-angle** (cone) — no local rule exists. Measured, a 3–4 facet chain determines neither, while the whole face determines both to 0.01°. A cone is not locally seedable; reach it by promotion from a validated cylinder or leave it to the whole-region ladder.

Two things this buys you. First, it says the same thing your clause was reaching for — a vertex-sharing fan fails the *apex* clause — without the false positives, because it names the observable rather than a proxy for it. Second, it puts each guard in the vocabulary the DEVELOPMENT_PLAN already uses for the identifiability / validity / model-selection distinction, so a reader can tell which kind each one is.

## One structural note

Your seed requirements are written **per type** — a cylinder seed, a cone seed, a sphere seed. That puts the type decision at the point of least information, which is exactly where the measurements say it cannot be made: 496 of 652 true cylinders are also fitted by a sphere on their *full* support, so a 4-facet chain has no chance. The pipeline already avoids this — `compete_from_seed` grows every admissible type from one seed and picks by validated area. I'd recommend the section follow it: **one seed, all types, selection after growth**, with the admissibility clauses above gating which types are worth trying rather than which seeds are legal.

```bash
/// Starts are taken at a stride over the face so the sample is spread rather

/// how much SUPPORT a fit needs, not whether the patch strays.
fn patch_size_probe(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    truth_axis: ([f64; 3], [f64; 3]),
    is_cone: bool,
    model: &str,
    ref_idx: usize,
    kind: &str,
) {
    const SIZES: [usize; 10] = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 64];
    const STARTS: usize = 8;
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let (_, want_dir) = truth_axis;
    let want = unit(want_dir);
    let ang = |d: [f64; 3]| -> f64 {
        let d = unit(d);
        let c = [
            d[1] * want[2] - d[2] * want[1],
            d[2] * want[0] - d[0] * want[2],
            d[0] * want[1] - d[1] * want[0],
        ];
        norm(c).clamp(0.0, 1.0).asin().to_degrees()
    };
    let stride = (faces.len() / STARTS).max(1);
    for &start in faces.iter().step_by(stride).take(STARTS) {
        // One BFS from the start, recording the axis error each time the
        // accumulated patch reaches the next size on the ladder.
        let mut patch = vec![start];
        let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([start]);
        let mut frontier = vec![start];
        let mut next_size = 0usize;
        while next_size < SIZES.len() {
            while next_size < SIZES.len() && patch.len() >= SIZES[next_size] {
                let target = SIZES[next_size];
                let sub: Vec<usize> = patch[..target.min(patch.len())].to_vec();
                let got = if is_cone {
                    super::initialize::cone(&sub, mesh, 5e-5)
                } else {
                    super::initialize::cylinder(&sub, mesh)
                };
                if let Some(
                    super::initialize::Initial::Cylinder { axis_dir, .. }
                    | super::initialize::Initial::Cone { axis_dir, .. },
                ) = got
                {
                    println!(
                        "PATCHSIZE\t{model}\t{ref_idx}\t{kind}\t{target}\t{:.6}",
                        ang(axis_dir)
                    );
                }
                next_size += 1;
            }
            // Expand one ring.
            let mut ring = Vec::new();
            for &fi in &frontier {
                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
                for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                    if ni < 0 {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nj = ni as usize;
                    if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                        patch.push(nj);
                        ring.push(nj);
                    }
                }
            }
            if ring.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            frontier = ring;
        }
    }
}
```

```bash
new = r'''// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The clean grow operator, and its basin of attraction
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Refit-and-reflood rounds before the clean operator gives up.
const MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS: usize = 12;

/// What happened when a seed SET was grown under the clean operator.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum Basin {
    /// Converged to exactly the reference face. The seed is in the basin.
    Exact,
    /// Converged to a strict subset — the fit stalled inside its own surface.
    Short,
    /// Converged to a strict superset — the fit leaked past the true boundary.
    Leak,
    /// Converged to something that is neither.
    Other,
    /// No fit of this type exists on the seed set (or on some later support).
    NoFit,
    /// The fit of the seed set does not validate any facet of the seed set.
    SeedRejected,
    /// Still moving at the round cap.
    NoConverge,
}

impl Basin {
    fn code(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Basin::Exact => 0,
            Basin::Short => 1,
            Basin::Leak => 2,
            Basin::Other => 3,
            Basin::NoFit => 4,
            Basin::SeedRejected => 5,
            Basin::NoConverge => 6,
        }
    }
}

/// **The clean operator.** `F₀ = S`; `F_{k+1}` = the union of the validated
/// components containing the seed set, under a fresh least-squares fit of
/// `F_k`; iterate to a fixpoint.
///
/// No `seed_patch`, no `condition_patch`, no trimming, no jet — the seed set is
/// the entire initial fit support and validation is the only thing that decides
/// membership. This is the baseline the Invariants section is trying to
/// establish, so the question "which seed sets are valid" becomes "which seed
/// sets lie in the basin of attraction of their own surface", which is what
/// this measures.
///
/// Growth is confined to the smooth region, as the pipeline does: the sharp
/// partition is the one thing measured exact, so leaving it in place isolates
/// the seeding question from the partitioning one.
fn grow_clean<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: &[usize],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> (Basin, Vec<usize>, usize, bool) {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let mut cur: Vec<usize> = seed.to_vec();
    cur.sort_unstable();
    let mut self_ok = false;
    for round in 0..MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS {
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &cur);
        let Some(mut fit) = S::fit_surface(mesh, &cur, &verts, 0) else {
            return (Basin::NoFit, cur, round, self_ok);
        };
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &cur, &mut fit);
        if round == 0 {
            // Does the seed set's own fit explain the whole seed set? A
            // ground-truth-free predicate, so it could gate admission in
            // production.
            self_ok = seed
                .iter()
                .all(|&fi| compete::face_validates::<S>(mesh, fi, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol));
        }
        let mut next: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
        for &st in seed {
            if next.contains(&st) {
                continue;
            }
            let comp = compete::flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, st, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
            next.extend(comp);
        }
        if next.is_empty() {
            return (Basin::SeedRejected, cur, round, self_ok);
        }
        let mut nv: Vec<usize> = next.into_iter().collect();
        nv.sort_unstable();
        if nv == cur {
            return (Basin::Exact, cur, round, self_ok); // caller re-classifies
        }
        cur = nv;
    }
    (Basin::NoConverge, cur, MAX_CLEAN_ROUNDS, self_ok)
}

/// Classify a converged result against the reference face.
fn classify(result: &[usize], truth: &HashSet<usize>) -> Basin {
    let inside = result.iter().filter(|f| truth.contains(f)).count();
    if inside == result.len() && result.len() == truth.len() {
        Basin::Exact
    } else if inside == result.len() {
        Basin::Short
    } else if inside == truth.len() {
        Basin::Leak
    } else {
        Basin::Other
    }
}

/// How large does a fit support have to be before it determines a developable?'''
```

```bash
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn basin_probe<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    faces: &[usize],
    truth: &HashSet<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    truth_axis: Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])>,

                let z = dot(w, tdir);
                let rad = sub(w, [tdir[0] * z, tdir[1] * z, tdir[2] * z]);
                let (x, y) = (dot(rad, bu), dot(rad, bv));
                let rr = x.hypot(y);
                if rr > 1e-12 {
                    angles.push(y.atan2(x));
                }
                zmin = zmin.min(z);
                zmax = zmax.max(z);
                rmax = rmax.max(rr);
            }
        }
        if angles.len() < 2 || rmax <= 0.0 {
            return (0.0, 0.0);
        }
        angles.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
        let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
        for w in angles.windows(2) {
            gap = gap.max(w[1] - w[0]);
        }
        (
            (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0).to_degrees(),
            (zmax - zmin) / rmax,
        )
    };

    let stride = (faces.len() / STARTS).max(1);
    let starts: Vec<usize> = faces.iter().copied().step_by(stride).take(STARTS).collect();
    let far = *faces.last().unwrap();
    for &start in &starts {
        for &k in &SIZES {
            if k > faces.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut cases: Vec<(&str, Vec<usize>)> = vec![("ball", ball(start, k))];
            if k >= 4 {
                let mut sp = ball(start, k / 2);
                sp.extend(ball(far, k - k / 2));
                sp.sort_unstable();
                sp.dedup();
                cases.push(("split", sp));
            }
            {
                let i0 = faces.iter().position(|&f| f == start).unwrap_or(0);
                let strip: Vec<usize> =
                    faces.iter().cycle().skip(i0).take(k).copied().collect();
                let mut st = strip;
                st.sort_unstable();
                st.dedup();
                cases.push(("strip", st));
            }
            for (shape, set) in cases {
                if set.len() < 2 {
                    continue;
                }
                let connected = is_connected(mesh, &set);
                let (sweep, axial) = spread(&set);
                let (mut verdict, result, rounds, self_ok) =
                    grow_clean::<S>(mesh, in_region, &set, centroids, config);
                if verdict == Basin::Exact {
                    verdict = classify(&result, truth);
                }
                let inside = result.iter().filter(|f| truth.contains(f)).count();
                let jacc = if result.is_empty() && truth.is_empty() {
                    1.0
                } else {
                    inside as f64 / (result.len() + truth.len() - inside).max(1) as f64
                };
                println!(
                    "BASIN\t{model}\t{ref_idx}\t{kind}\t{}\t{shape}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t\
                     {sweep:.3}\t{axial:.5}\t{jacc:.4}\t{}",
                    faces.len(),
                    set.len(),
                    u8::from(connected),
                    u8::from(self_ok),
                    verdict.code(),
                    rounds,
                    result.len(),
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Is a facet set connected through the mesh's face adjacency?
fn is_connected(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, set: &[usize]) -> bool {
    if set.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    let member: HashSet<usize> = set.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([set[0]]);
    let mut stack = vec![set[0]];
    while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let nj = ni as usize;
            if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                stack.push(nj);
            }
        }
    }
    seen.len() == set.len()
}

/// How large does a fit support have to be before it determines a developable?'''
```

> So with the clean operator applied—no seed or condition patches—and filtering for seed sets that pass the self-consistency check with at least 8 facets, the invariant holds remarkably well across most geometries: the plane achieves perfect coverage, the cylinder and sphere both stay above 90%, but the cone drops to 61%, and the torus is significantly lower at just under 17%.
> 
> The real issue isn't seed selection—it's that the torus systematically overshoots by about 4%, growing a row or two past where it should stop at the tangent junction. This happens consistently across all seed sets, which means no amount of refining what counts as a "valid seed" will solve it. The problem is fundamentally about the boundary criterion itself: when the fit tolerance allows vertices to be within tolerance of both the torus and the adjacent cylinder near their tangency, the growth algorithm naturally extends too far. The user needs either a mechanism to handle tangent boundaries explicitly, or a different stopping criterion altogether—not just better seed selection.
> 
> That said, there's an important distinction: if the pipeline keeps multi-claiming and uses `resolve_claims` to arbitrate overlaps, then the torus leaking 4% into rows that another surface claims better is actually benign and expected. The growth invariant would need to be reframed as "covers at least the surface, with overshoots only into rows another surface claims better" rather than "covers exactly." That's the key design recommendation to give the user.
> 
> For cones specifically, the results show 50% exact fits but 35% fail at the fit or seed validation stage. Even with `self_ok` enabled and k≥8, I'm only getting 61% coverage—cones need larger seeds than what I tested, probably in the 24–64 facet range based on the earlier patch-size curve.
> 
> Interestingly, whether the seed is connected or split doesn't matter much; disconnected seeds actually perform slightly better at 82.3%. The real lever here is `self_ok` as the admission predicate—it jumps success from 0.4% to 84.6%, and it's ground-truth-free and threshold-free since it reuses existing tolerances. Though I should note `self_ok` is necessary but not sufficient; it's related to but distinct from SeedRejected, which fires when the flood validates no seed members at all.
> 
> Now I'm drafting a concrete definition: a valid seed set S for type T requires that the fitter produces parameters and every facet in S validates against those parameters at vertex tolerance. Nothing about connectivity, size, coplanarity, or facet count. This definition alone pushes success to 84.6%, and combined with the size floor (|S| ≥ 8) I'm seeing 100/92/91% per-face agreement for plane/cylinder/sphere. Though for small seeds like 2-facet cylinders, condition (2) becomes almost tautological—the fit naturally validates its own input—so the size floor is doing separate work, and that floor varies by shape type.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CdkYVVxGoBGsfAq5mHM47 -->

Here's the answer to the design question, measured rather than argued. I built the clean operator you describe — `F₀ = S`, `F_{k+1}` = validated component(s) containing S under a fresh least-squares fit of `F_k`, iterate to fixpoint — with no `seed_patch`, no `condition_patch`, no trimming, no jet. Then I grew **87 510 seed sets over 897 reference faces / 107 models**: 8 sizes × 3 shapes × 5 start positions per face, every seed set drawn entirely from inside one true surface.

## The definition that works

> **A set S of facets is a valid seed for type T iff `fit_T(S)` exists and every facet of S validates that fit at vertex tolerance.**

That's it. Nothing about connectivity, vertex counts, coplanarity, or fit accuracy.

| | seed sets | grew to exactly the surface |
|---|---|---|
| fails the predicate | 5 046 | **0.4%** |
| passes it | 82 464 | **84.6%** |

The failures below the line are 64% "the fit doesn't explain its own seed" and 30% "no fit exists" — i.e. the predicate catches exactly the two ways a seed can be hopeless, and nothing else.

What makes it the right shape rather than one more heuristic: it is **the fixpoint condition itself, evaluated at round 0**. The property you want at the end — `F = flood(fit(F))` — applied at the start is `S ⊆ flood(fit(S))`. Admission and termination become one predicate at two scales, and it introduces no new constant (it reuses `vtol`/`stol`).

Adding a size floor of 8 facets, per reference face — *every* admissible seed set converging to the same, correct answer:

| type | faces | all seeds exact | all seeds agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| plane | 145 | **100.0%** | 100.0% |
| cylinder | 379 | **92.3%** | 94.5% |
| sphere | 139 | **91.4%** | 92.8% |
| cone | 41 | 61.0% | 70.7% |
| torus | 125 | **16.8%** | 61.6% |

For comparison, the current pipeline (single seed facet + `seed_patch` + `condition_patch`) gives full seed-agreement on **34.9%** of surfaces. So the clean baseline is not a regression to be defended — for planes, cylinders and spheres it is substantially better than what exists.

## Your instincts confirmed

- **A bad fit really is good enough.** Cylinders: 74.9% at |S| = 2, **91.5% at |S| = 3**, plateau ~95% by 12. A 3-facet seed with a 1° axis error still converges, because the refit fixes it. The seed does not need to be accurate, only *determining*.
- **Connectivity is not required.** Connected 79.6%, disconnected 80.1%. The best-performing shape was `split` — two BFS balls at the two most distant points of the surface (82.3%, only 25% connected) — which is also the well-conditioned shape for an axis. That's a real design freedom worth writing into the definition explicitly, since "chain" implies otherwise.
- **Shape barely matters**: ball 78.4%, split 82.3%, strip 79.3%. Including the ruling-walking `strip`, which was fatal in Phase 1.2 — because there it fed a *one-shot* fit, and here the refit loop recovers.

## Two walls no seed definition can move

**1. Tori leak, and they leak seed-independently.** 45.6% of all torus seed sets converge to the surface *plus a collar*: overshoot p50 **1.04×**, p95 1.12, max 1.20. And 62% of torus faces have every admissible seed landing within 2% of the *same* answer. So growth is already seed-independent there — it simply does not stop at the true boundary. Past a tangent junction the neighbour's facets are within `vtol` of the torus because tangency means second-order agreement. **This is a boundary problem, not a seeding problem**, and no definition of "valid seed set" reaches it.

**2. Cones cannot be seeded small.** At the sizes sampled, 21% SeedRejected + 14% NoFit. The support-size curve says a cone's axis needs 24–64 facets to get under a degree, against ~16 for a cylinder. A cone should be reached by promotion from a validated cylinder, not seeded locally.

## What I'd change in the invariant's wording

Keep the definition above, and **change the target of the growth invariant** from "covers the surface exactly" to:

> **Growth invariant.** For every valid seed set S ⊆ F, the fixpoint of grow-with-refit **contains F**, and overshoots only into facets that a neighbouring surface explains strictly better.

Measured, "all admissible seeds cover the truth" reads 100 / 95.3 / 92.8 / 63.4 / **60.8%** for plane / cylinder / sphere / cone / torus, against "exactly" at 100 / 92.3 / 91.4 / 61.0 / **16.8%**. The entire torus gap is the collar.

That formulation is achievable, it preserves seed independence, and it puts the boundary decision where the information actually is — a *comparison between two surfaces*, not a threshold inside one. Which means the clean baseline should eliminate `seed_patch` and `condition_patch` (the measurements support that) but **keep multi-claiming and `resolve_claims`** (the measurements say the collar is unavoidable without them).

## Caveats

Growth stayed confined to the smooth region — I kept the sharp partition, since it's the one thing measured exact, so this isolates seeding from partitioning. The surface *type* was given by ground truth; type discovery is a separate question and my earlier numbers say residual can't answer it. Cone n = 41 faces is thin. Sampling is 5 starts × 8 sizes × 3 shapes per face, not exhaustive. And I haven't re-run the suite since these diagnostic additions — all of it sits behind `--invariant-report` and `BREPPER_INV_BASIN=1`, but it's unverified.

Every overshoot facet in the corpus is in a face adjacent to the one that grew, and every one that can be measured is closer to its true owner's surface than to the fit that claimed it. So `resolve_claims` is handed exactly the information your invariant promises it — the boundary decision is a comparison between two surfaces, and the comparison always points the right way.

(The sphere row is a real gap, not a pass: sphere overshoots land on freeform neighbours, which have no closed-form distance, so I couldn't score them. 145 plane faces never overshot at all.)

## How much collar resolution has to absorb

Median |result| / |truth| is **1.000** for plane, cylinder, cone and sphere. Only tori carry a real collar: median **1.019**, p95 **1.117**, max 1.20. So the work is bounded at roughly a 2% median / 12% tail overgrowth on fillets, and nothing anywhere else.

## What's left

At floor 16 the residual is **cones (83.8%)** and **tori (83.2%)**. Cones mostly fail as `NoFit` — the fitter declines the support entirely, consistent with the earlier support-size curve saying a cone's axis needs 24–64 facets. Tori fail as `SeedRejected` and `Short`.

Stalls — the one failure mode that genuinely breaks the invariant — are only **1.70%** of admissible seeds at floor 8, and they are mostly a seed property rather than a face property: 60 faces have *some* seeds stall while others succeed, against only 7 where every seed stalls. Almost all of them are `stepped_block_toroidal`, the corpus's known narrow-flat-region pathology. When a seed does stall it stalls badly (median shortfall 47% of the face), so this is a distinct failure to detect, not a near-miss to tolerate.

And one finding worth building into the definition: **spread seeds beat compact ones.** Stall rate by shape — `split` (two distant balls, mostly disconnected) 1.02%, `ball` 1.48%, `strip` 2.56%; by connectivity — disconnected 0.67%, connected 2.46%. So not only is connectivity not required, requiring it would make the invariant *worse*.

## Suggested wording

> **Valid seed set.** A set S of facets is a valid seed for surface type T iff `fit_T(S)` exists, every facet of S validates it at vertex tolerance, and |S| ≥ 16. S need not be connected, and a spread seed is preferred to a compact one.
>
> **Growth invariant.** For every valid seed set S contained in a surface F, grow-with-refit converges to a set that **contains F**, and every facet it adds beyond F belongs to a reference-adjacent surface that explains that facet strictly better.

Measured: 95.0% of reference faces satisfy the first part for *every* admissible seed; the second part holds on 100% of overshoot facets.

## Caveats

Growth stayed inside the smooth region (sharp partition retained). Surface *type* was given by ground truth — type discovery is a separate question, and my earlier measurement says residual magnitude cannot answer it. Sphere overshoot is unscored against the second clause. Cone n = 41 faces is thin. Sampling was 5 starts × 8 sizes × 3 shapes per face — 87 510 grows over 897 faces / 107 models — not exhaustive. /// Seed green; covered blue; overshoot red; missed yellow; blocked orange.
```bash
const C_SEED: [f32; 4] = [0.15, 0.85, 0.25, 1.0];
const C_COVERED: [f32; 4] = [0.20, 0.45, 0.95, 1.0];

const C_BLOCKED: [f32; 4] = [1.00, 0.55, 0.05, 1.0];

/// A deterministic 64-bit mixer, so a "random" seed set is reproducible from
/// the model name, reference index and sample number.
fn splitmix64(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
    *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    let mut z = *state;
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
    z ^ (z >> 31)
}

/// One seed set to show, with everything needed to explain its outcome.
struct SeedCase {
    shape: &'static str,
    seed: Vec<usize>,
    verdict: Basin,
    result: Vec<usize>,
    rounds: usize,
    self_ok: bool,
    /// Truth facets the growth never reached.
    missed: Vec<usize>,
    /// Result facets outside the truth.
    overshoot: Vec<usize>,
    /// Missed truth facets that touch the result — the ones that actually
    /// stopped it — each with the factor by which it failed vertex tolerance.
    blocked: Vec<(usize, f64)>,
    /// The worst vertex distance of the seed set to its OWN first fit, in units
    /// of vertex tolerance. > 1 means the seed does not lie on its own fit.
    seed_self_ratio: f64,
}

impl SeedCase {
    fn covers(&self) -> bool {
        self.missed.is_empty() && !matches!(self.verdict, Basin::NoFit | Basin::SeedRejected)
    }
    /// A one-line diagnosis, in the vocabulary of what went wrong.
    fn why(&self, n_truth: usize) -> String {
        match self.verdict {
            Basin::NoFit => format!(
                "NO FIT — the fitter declines a {}-facet support outright (under-determined)",
                self.seed.len()
            ),
            Basin::SeedRejected => format!(
                "SEED REJECTED — the seed's own fit misses its own facets by {:.1}x vertex \
                 tolerance, so nothing floods",
                self.seed_self_ratio
            ),
            Basin::Short => {
                let best = self
                    .blocked
                    .iter()
                    .map(|&(_, r)| r)
                    .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
                format!(
                    "STALLED — reached {}/{} facets; {} true facet(s) on the frontier failed \
                     validation, the closest by {:.1}x vertex tolerance",
                    self.result.len(),
                    n_truth,
                    self.blocked.len(),
                    best
                )
            }
            Basin::Leak => format!(
                "COVERS + OVERSHOOT — {}/{} true facets plus {} beyond the true boundary",
                self.result.len() - self.overshoot.len(),
                n_truth,
                self.overshoot.len()
            ),
            Basin::Other => format!(
                "MIXED — {} true facets missed AND {} claimed beyond the boundary",
                self.missed.len(),
                self.overshoot.len()
            ),
            Basin::NoConverge => format!(
                "NO FIXPOINT — still moving after {} refit rounds ({} facets)",
                self.rounds,
                self.result.len()
            ),
            Basin::Exact => format!("EXACT — {} facets, {} refit round(s)", n_truth, self.rounds),
        }
    }
}

/// Build the seed sets to show for one reference face, in the shapes and sizes
/// the CLI asked for.
fn viz_seed_sets(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
    model: &str,
    ref_idx: usize,
) -> Vec<(&'static str, Vec<usize>)> {
    let member: HashSet<usize> = faces.iter().copied().collect();
    let ball = |start: usize, k: usize| -> Vec<usize> {
        let mut out = vec![start];
        let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::from([start]);
        let mut frontier = vec![start];
        while out.len() < k && !frontier.is_empty() {
            let mut ring = Vec::new();
            for &fi in &frontier {
                let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
                for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                    if ni < 0 || out.len() >= k {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nj = ni as usize;
                    if member.contains(&nj) && seen.insert(nj) {
                        out.push(nj);
                        ring.push(nj);
                    }
                }
            }
            if ring.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            frontier = ring;
        }
        out.sort_unstable();
        out
    };
    let want = |name: &str| config.viz_seed_shapes.iter().any(|s| s == name);
    let mut rng = model
        .bytes()
        .fold(0x243F_6A88_85A3_08D3_u64, |a, b| a.rotate_left(7) ^ b as u64)
        ^ (ref_idx as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    let mut out: Vec<(&'static str, Vec<usize>)> = Vec::new();
    for &k in &config.viz_seed_sizes {
        if k < 1 || k > faces.len() {
            continue;
        }
        for sample in 0..config.viz_seed_samples.max(1) {
            let start = faces[(splitmix64(&mut rng) as usize) % faces.len()];
            if want("ball") {
                out.push(("ball", ball(start, k)));
            }
            if want("split") && k >= 2 {
                let other = faces[(splitmix64(&mut rng) as usize) % faces.len()];
                let mut sp = ball(start, k / 2 + k % 2);
                sp.extend(ball(other, k / 2));
                sp.sort_unstable();
                sp.dedup();
                out.push(("split", sp));
            }
            if want("strip") {
                let i0 = faces.iter().position(|&f| f == start).unwrap_or(0);
                let mut st: Vec<usize> =
                    faces.iter().cycle().skip(i0).take(k).copied().collect();
                st.sort_unstable();
                st.dedup();
                out.push(("strip", st));
            }
            if want("random") {
                // Uniform without replacement — deliberately allowed to be
                // disconnected and scattered, which the measurements say is
                // legitimate (disconnected seeds stall LESS often).
                let mut pool: Vec<usize> = faces.to_vec();
                let mut pick = Vec::new();
                for _ in 0..k.min(pool.len()) {
                    let j = (splitmix64(&mut rng) as usize) % pool.len();
                    pick.push(pool.swap_remove(j));
                }
                pick.sort_unstable();
                out.push(("random", pick));
            }
            let _ = sample;
        }
    }
    out.retain(|(_, s)| !s.is_empty());
    out
}

/// Grow one seed set and work out, in detail, what happened to it.
fn diagnose<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: &[usize],
    truth: &HashSet<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    shape: &'static str,
) -> SeedCase {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let (mut verdict, result, rounds, self_ok, fit) =
        grow_clean::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, centroids, config);
    if verdict == Basin::Exact {
        verdict = classify(&result, truth);
    }
    let rset: HashSet<usize> = result.iter().copied().collect();
    let mut missed: Vec<usize> = truth.difference(&rset).copied().collect();
    let mut overshoot: Vec<usize> = rset.difference(truth).copied().collect();
    missed.sort_unstable();
    overshoot.sort_unstable();

    // Which of the missed facets actually blocked growth: the ones touching the
    // result. Their distance to the final fit, in units of vertex tolerance, is
    // the answer to "why did it stop here".
    let mut blocked: Vec<(usize, f64)> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(f) = fit.as_ref() {
        for &m in &missed {
            let vc = mesh.faces[m].vertex_count as usize;
            let touches = mesh.faces[m].neighbors[..vc]
                .iter()
                .any(|&ni| ni >= 0 && rset.contains(&(ni as usize)));
            if !touches {
                continue;
            }
            let worst = facet_points(mesh, m)
                .iter()
                .map(|p| S::vertex_distance(f, p))
                .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
            blocked.push((m, worst / vtol.max(1e-30)));
        }
    }
    blocked.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(&b.1).unwrap());

    // How far the seed sits from its own first fit — the admission quantity.
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, seed);
    let seed_self_ratio = match S::fit_surface(mesh, seed, &verts, 0) {
        Some(mut f0) => {
            S::determine_convexity(mesh, seed, &mut f0);
            let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
            for &fi in seed {
                for p in facet_points(mesh, fi) {
                    worst = worst.max(S::vertex_distance(&f0, &p));
                }
                let _ = compete::face_validates::<S>(mesh, fi, &f0, centroids, vtol, stol);
            }
            worst / vtol.max(1e-30)
        }
        None => f64::NAN,
    };

    SeedCase {
        shape,
        seed: seed.to_vec(),
        verdict,
        result,
        rounds,
        self_ok,
        missed,
        overshoot,
        blocked,
        seed_self_ratio,
    }
}

/// Interactive walk over sampled seed sets, stopping on the ones the CLI's
/// `--viz-seed-show` selects. Returns false when the user quits.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn viz_face<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    faces: &[usize],
    truth: &HashSet<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    viz: &crate::viz::VizSender,
    model: &str,
    ref_idx: usize,
    kind: &str,
) -> bool {
    let show = config.viz_seed_show.as_str();
    for (shape, set) in viz_seed_sets(mesh, faces, config, model, ref_idx) {
        let case = diagnose::<S>(mesh, in_region, &set, truth, centroids, config, shape);
        let wanted = match show {
            "all" => true,
            "covering" => case.covers(),
            _ => !case.covers(),
        };
        if !wanted {
            continue;
        }
        let mut ov = crate::viz::VizOverlay::new();
        let rset: HashSet<usize> = case.result.iter().copied().collect();
        let covered: Vec<usize> = case
            .result
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|f| truth.contains(f) && !case.seed.contains(f))
            .collect();
        let blocked_only: Vec<usize> = case.blocked.iter().map(|&(f, _)| f).collect();
        let missed_only: Vec<usize> = case
            .missed
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|f| !blocked_only.contains(f))
            .collect();
        for (idxs, color) in [
            (covered, C_COVERED),
            (case.overshoot.clone(), C_OVERSHOOT),
            (missed_only, C_MISSED),
            (blocked_only, C_BLOCKED),
            (case.seed.clone(), C_SEED),
        ] {
            if !idxs.is_empty() {
                ov.face_highlights.push(crate::viz::FaceHighlight {
                    face_indices: idxs,
                    color,
                });
            }
        }
        let c = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[case.seed[0]], &mesh.vertices);
        ov.focus_point = Some([c[0] as f32, c[1] as f32, c[2] as f32]);
        let n = facet_normal(mesh, case.seed[0]);
        ov.focus_normal = Some([n[0] as f32, n[1] as f32, n[2] as f32]);
        ov.status_text = format!(
            "{model} ref#{ref_idx} {kind} ({} facets) | seed {} x{} | self-fit {:.2}x vtol{} | {}",
            faces.len(),
            case.shape,
            case.seed.len(),
            case.seed_self_ratio,
            if case.self_ok { "" } else { " (FAILS admission)" },
            case.why(truth.len()),
        );
        let _ = rset;
        match viz.show_and_wait(ov) {
            crate::viz::VizAction::Quit => return false,
            crate::viz::VizAction::NextSeed => return true,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    true
}
```

```bash
///
/// `face_validates` is a conjunction of three tests — vertex distance, centroid
/// distance, and orientation coherence — and a diagnosis that reports only the
/// first is actively misleading: a facet can sit exactly on the surface (0.00x
/// vertex tolerance) and still be refused for the other two. Both of those
/// happen in the corpus.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct FacetVerdict {
    /// Worst vertex distance, in units of `--vertex-tolerance`.
    vratio: f64,
    /// Centroid distance, in units of `--surface-tolerance`.
    cratio: f64,
    /// Does the facet normal agree in sign with the surface normal?
    orient: bool,
}

impl FacetVerdict {
    fn ok(&self) -> bool {
        self.orient && self.vratio <= 1.0 && self.cratio <= 1.0
    }
    /// The clause that refused this facet, and by how much.
    fn cause(&self) -> String {
        if !self.orient {
            "ORIENTATION (facet normal opposes the surface)".to_string()
        } else if self.vratio > 1.0 && self.cratio > 1.0 {
            format!(
                "VERTEX {:.1}x vtol and CENTROID {:.1}x stol",
                self.vratio, self.cratio
            )
        } else if self.vratio > 1.0 {
            format!("VERTEX {:.1}x vtol", self.vratio)
        } else if self.cratio > 1.0 {
            format!("CENTROID {:.1}x stol", self.cratio)
        } else {
            "nothing (it passes)".to_string()
        }
    }
}

fn facet_verdict<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    fi: usize,
    fit: &S::Fit,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
) -> FacetVerdict {
    let vratio = facet_points(mesh, fi)
        .iter()
        .map(|p| S::vertex_distance(fit, p))
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
        / vtol.max(1e-30);
    FacetVerdict {
        vratio,
        cratio: S::centroid_distance(fit, &centroids[fi]) / stol.max(1e-30),
        orient: S::convexity_check(fit, mesh, fi),
    }
}

/// Summarise a set of facet verdicts into one dominant cause.
fn dominant_cause(vs: &[(usize, FacetVerdict)]) -> String {
    let bad: Vec<&(usize, FacetVerdict)> = vs.iter().filter(|(_, v)| !v.ok()).collect();
    if bad.is_empty() {
        return "nothing — every facet passes".to_string();
    }
    let (orient, vtx, cent) = (
        bad.iter().filter(|(_, v)| !v.orient).count(),
        bad.iter().filter(|(_, v)| v.orient && v.vratio > 1.0).count(),
        bad.iter()
            .filter(|(_, v)| v.orient && v.vratio <= 1.0 && v.cratio > 1.0)
            .count(),
    );
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    if orient > 0 {
        parts.push(format!("{orient} on ORIENTATION"));
    }
    if vtx > 0 {
        let worst = bad
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, v)| v.orient && v.vratio > 1.0)
            .map(|(_, v)| v.vratio)
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let closest = bad
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, v)| v.orient && v.vratio > 1.0)
            .map(|(_, v)| v.vratio)
            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
        parts.push(format!(
            "{vtx} on VERTEX ({closest:.1}x-{worst:.1}x vtol)"
        ));
    }
    if cent > 0 {
        let worst = bad
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, v)| v.orient && v.vratio <= 1.0 && v.cratio > 1.0)
            .map(|(_, v)| v.cratio)
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        parts.push(format!("{cent} on CENTROID (up to {worst:.1}x stol)"));
    }
    parts.join(", ")
}
```

## The viz mode

`--viz-seeds` grows sampled seed sets under the clean operator and stops on each one you asked to see. Colours: **green** seed · **blue** correctly covered · **red** overshoot · **orange** true facets that *blocked* further growth · **yellow** true facets missed for other reasons. Controls are the existing ones — `Space` next seed set, `Shift+Space` next reference face, `Q` quit. The status line above the window (also on stderr as `[viz]`) carries the diagnosis.


Flags: `--viz-seed-show=failing|all|covering` (default `failing`), `--viz-seed-sizes`, `--viz-seed-shapes=ball,split,strip,random`, `--viz-seed-samples`. `random` draws uniformly from the surface and is deliberately allowed to be scattered. `BREPPER_VIZ_SEEDS_TEXT=1` gives the same diagnoses as text with no window.

## Building it changed two of my earlier answers

**My diagnostic was lying, and fixing it exposed a cause I'd never separated.** `face_validates` is a conjunction of *three* tests — vertex distance, centroid distance, orientation coherence — and I had only been measuring the first. That produced self-contradictory messages ("fails admission at 0.00× vtol"). Now every verdict names the clause. Of the seeds refused by their own fit, **7% pass the vertex test** and are thrown out by centroid or orientation instead.

**And 10% of all failures are not seeding failures at all.** Chasing one nonsensical message — "reached 432/433, 0 facets refused" — found that the missing facet was in a *different smooth region*. Stage 2.1 had called an edge sharp inside the true torus, so the flood is confined and **no seed set can ever reach the rest of the surface**. That's the A-family measurement from earlier (350 sharp edges inside 68 true surfaces) showing up as a growth failure. It now reports as its own category, `CUT BY THE PARTITION`.

## Why seeds fail at sizes 2/3/4

43 056 seed sets, 897 reference faces, 107 models. **82.9% cover their surface; 7 384 fail:**

| share of failures | cause |
|---|---|
| **35.8%** | the seed set's own fit refuses its own facets |
| **29.9%** | stalled — frontier true facets refused on vertex tolerance |
| **21.3%** | no fit of that type exists on the seed set (under-determined) |
| **10.0%** | cut by the partition — the rest is in another region |
| 2.4% | stalled — frontier refused on **orientation** |
| 0.6% | no fixpoint within 12 refit rounds |

By type, at your sizes:

| type | n | cover | no fit | seed refused | partition-cut | stalled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plane | 7 200 | **99.9%** | 0.0% | 0.1% | 0.0% | 0.1% |
| sphere | 6 672 | **92.3%** | 0.1% | 0.0% | 7.2% | 0.5% |
| cylinder | 21 216 | **91.7%** | 0.9% | 0.1% | 0.9% | 6.5% |
| torus | 6 000 | **37.1%** | 19.2% | 33.1% | 1.0% | 42.2% |
| cone | 1 968 | **32.5%** | 11.7% | 31.5% | 2.4% | 53.3% |

So at 2–4 facets the story is entirely about cones and tori, and it is dominated by the seed set being unable to describe itself: a 2–4 facet support either admits no 6/7-DOF fit at all, or admits one that misses its own facets by a median of **167× vertex tolerance** (p95 2 906×, max 129 546×). Those are the red/orange frames you'll see.

Spheres are the interesting middle: 92.3% cover, and their *only* real failure mode is partition-cut at 7.2% — nothing wrong with the seeds, the surface was already severed.

The admission predicate still earns its place: 91% of seed sets at these sizes pass it, and of those **91.5% cover** against 82.9% unfiltered.

```bash
fn vertex_star_map(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> HashMap<usize, Vec<usize>> {

fn star_is_complete(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, vi: usize, star: &[usize], member: &HashSet<usize>) -> bool {

    // that is not itself in `member` means the ring is cut by the boundary.

fn connected_subsets_containing(

    let mut seen: HashSet<Vec<usize>> = HashSet::new();
    let mut frontier: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![vec![anchor]];
    for _ in 1..max_n {

            break;

fn is_chain(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, set: &[usize]) -> bool {

        return false;

        }

            ends += 1;
        }

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn seed_family(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    member: &HashSet<usize>,
    vstar: &HashMap<usize, Vec<usize>>,
    kind: Kind,
    anchor: usize,
    max_chain: usize,
    require_coplanar_clause: bool,

) -> Vec<(&'static str, Vec<usize>)> {

    let copl_rel = 1.0e-6;

        Kind::Plane => out.push(("facet", vec![anchor])),
        Kind::Cylinder | Kind::Cone => {
            for set in connected_subsets_containing(mesh, member, anchor, max_chain, cap * 8) {
                let vs = vertices_of(mesh, &set);
                if vs.len() != 6 || !is_chain(mesh, &set) {

                if require_coplanar_clause {
                    let pts: Vec<[f64; 3]> = vs.iter().map(|&v| vertex_pos(mesh, v)).collect();
                    if any_four_coplanar(&pts, copl_rel) {

                    }
                }
                out.push(("chain6", set));
                if out.len() >= cap {
                    break;
                }
            }
            if kind == Kind::Cone {
                // Three triangles sharing a vertex — the apex alternative.
                let vc = mesh.faces[anchor].vertex_count as usize;
                for &vi in &mesh.faces[anchor].vertex_indices[..vc] {
                    let star = &vstar[&vi];
                    let tris: Vec<usize> = star

                        pick.sort_unstable();
                        out.push(("apex3", pick));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Kind::Sphere => {
            let ring = |f: usize| -> Vec<usize> {
                let mut r = vec![f];
                let vc = mesh.faces[f].vertex_count as usize;
                for &ni in &mesh.faces[f].neighbors[..vc] {
                    if ni >= 0 && member.contains(&(ni as usize)) {

            out.push(("edge-ring", ring(anchor)));

                if out.len() >= cap {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        Kind::Other => {}
    }
    out.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.cmp(&b.1));
    out.dedup_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1);
    out
```

```bash
fn probe_anchor<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
```
